Many stores have cameras that watch customers to prevent shoplifting. But now, some retailers use new technology that can identify people's age, sex, size, and more without focusing on shoplifting. This technology uses cameras and computers to analyze facial features and compare them to a database.

A recent report said that about 30% of stores use this type of technology to track customers in-store. The goal is not to create detailed records of individual people's lives but to understand general shopping habits and behaviors.

For example, if a woman wearing a gold necklace walks quickly towards the sock aisle, a store can predict she might want to buy socks. This information can be used to show her targeted ads on screens in the store.

Some experts think that using this technology is not as bad as it seems because it doesn't collect personally identifiable information about individual customers. However, others feel that it's still invasive and creepy.

One company, Hoxton Analytics, has developed a system that uses machine learning and artificial intelligence to categorize people based on the shoes they wear. This can help retailers understand demographics without using facial recognition technology.

Retailers argue that this type of tracking is necessary to provide personalized shopping experiences for customers. However, some people still feel uncomfortable with the idea of being watched in stores.

Interestingly, a survey found that older people (55 and over) are more uncomfortable with these technologies than younger people (16-24). This might be because older people are less familiar with digital technology or because they have different expectations about how companies should treat their personal data.

Insects can be a good source of protein and food. They have been eaten in some parts of the world for a long time, but now people want to eat them more widely. A festival called Pestival 2013 will be held in London to promote eating insects. Some chefs think they taste good and are using them in their restaurants.

One restaurant called Noma in Denmark has already served ants and other insects to customers. The chef, René Redzepi, says that ants taste like lemon and that a purée of fermented grasshoppers tastes like fish sauce. Insects can be used as a substitute for eggs in cooking.

Eating insects could also help the environment because they produce fewer greenhouse gases than cows do. A group called the FAO has been working with countries in Asia and Africa to promote eating insects. They think it's a good idea because there are so many insects and they can be grown on organic waste.

Some experts believe that if people eat more insects, it could help reduce greenhouse gas emissions. In fact, one study suggested that swapping pork and beef for crickets and locusts could reduce emissions by as much as 95%. 

Insects are already being farmed in some countries, like China and Zimbabwe, where they are used as a food source. But in the UK, eating insects is not yet widely accepted.

There are many reasons why people should consider eating insects. They are a good source of protein, they can be grown on organic waste, and they produce fewer greenhouse gases than cows do. So, maybe it's time to give them a try!

The use of coal for energy may soon surpass oil, according to experts. This could have very bad effects on the environment.

One reason people are using more coal is that the US has been producing a lot of shale gas. Shale gas has made it cheaper to produce coal in other countries.

A report by the International Energy Agency (IEA) says that coal use is increasing all over the world, except in the US where shale gas has replaced it. This has made coal cheaper and more popular.

The IEA's director, Maria van der Hoeven, said: "Coal will soon be as important as oil if nothing changes." Coal is abundant and can be easily extracted from many parts of the world.

China and India are driving up demand for coal in the next five years. India may even become the second biggest user of coal in the world. China imports a lot of coal, while Indonesia exports it.

According to the IEA, the world will use 1.2 billion more tonnes of coal per year by 2017 than we do now. This is equivalent to the current coal consumption of Russia and the US combined.

Coal produces a lot of carbon dioxide emissions, which contribute to climate change. When coal is burned in old power plants, it can also produce pollutants like acid rain and soot particles.

Van der Hoeven said that without a high price for carbon dioxide emissions, people will keep using more coal. She suggested that making gas production more efficient could reduce demand for coal.

This has happened in the US, where shale gas production has increased. Van der Hoeven believes other countries like Europe and China should follow this example.

However, the Emissions Trading Scheme in Europe is not working as intended. It's supposed to discourage the use of high-carbon fuels like coal, but it's actually making coal more popular. This means that efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions are failing.

The world may face a higher risk of climate change if coal consumption continues to rise unchecked.

Many people know they don't get enough sleep, but a simple solution is to wake up later. Dr Paul Kelley from Oxford University suggested that schools change their starting times to match the natural body clocks of students. This would help them do better in class, have good grades, and be healthier.

Research has shown that children's bodies naturally want to wake up at different times as they get older. When they are 10 years old, they tend to wake up around 6:30am, but by the time they are 16 or 17, they want to sleep in until 8 or even 9am.

However, schools usually start classes too early for older teenagers. It's not just a matter of telling them to go to bed earlier. Dr Kelley explained that our bodies have an internal clock that is controlled by light, and it's hard to change.

This isn't just about students. Many people in their 20s and 30s lose over two hours of sleep each night because they need to wake up early for work or school. Even adults who are 50 years old or older tend to wake up naturally at around the same time as children when they were 10.

Dr Kelley thinks that workplaces should also change their schedules to fit our natural body clocks. For example, some people might start working later in the morning, while others might start earlier. This could have many positive effects, such as improving our mood and health, reducing accidents, and making us more productive.

Changing work hours might even reduce traffic congestion during rush hour. Dr Kelley thinks that a later start to the day would benefit everyone, especially families who often struggle with getting teenagers up early for school.

Dr Kelley himself wakes up naturally at around 6am, which is much easier than when he was younger. He believes that changing our work and school schedules could be a simple solution to many problems.

Felix Baumgartner stood at the edge of space over New Mexico. He was about to jump from a special capsule 24 miles above the ground. Mission control told him, "Our guardian angel will take care of you." Felix jumped into free fall.

It took 10 minutes for Felix to reach the Earth's surface. During this time, he reached speeds of up to 725mph and broke three world records. He became the first person to break the sound barrier while skydiving.

Felix was wearing a special suit that kept him safe from the extreme pressures during his fall. Without it, his blood would have boiled and his lungs might have exploded.

After two failed attempts, Felix finally jumped on Sunday morning. A huge balloon carried him up into clear skies. Felix went through a checklist of 40 items with his mentor Joe Kittinger before jumping.

There was some concern that Felix's visor was not working properly due to a broken heater. However, they decided to go ahead with the jump, which was watched by 8 million people online.

Felix reached speeds of over 700mph and broke three world records. He also set a new record for the longest free fall. Felix's team is now looking into how this technology can help astronauts in case of emergencies.

Felix has made a name for himself with his daring stunts. He has parachuted off buildings, mountains, and even into a 600-foot deep cave. This jump was seven years in the planning and sponsored by Red Bull drinks.

After the jump, Felix said he wants to inspire people and set up new records. He also mentioned that this will be his last big jump, as he plans to settle down with his girlfriend.

Barack Obama returned to Washington on Wednesday after giving an election victory speech in Chicago. He asked Americans to come together behind him, saying "You voted for action, not politics as usual." However, he may face a difficult time working with the Republican-led House of Representatives and Senate.

The President is unlikely to get a honeymoon period like he did after his first election in 2008. The Republican Speaker, John Boehner, and Democratic Leader in the Senate, Harry Reid, said they want to work together to solve problems. But this could be one of the biggest disagreements between Obama's administration and Congress.

Obama easily won the presidential election against Mitt Romney, but it showed how divided America remains. He will start his second term on Wednesday, January 20th, and wants to leave a good legacy. His goals include continuing economic recovery, improving education, and addressing climate change and immigration reform.

Boehner said there needs to be common ground between the parties to help the economy grow. Obama has already started talking with Boehner to negotiate. Reid also called for working together to solve problems.

Obama's team is optimistic about a "grand bargain" with Republicans, but talks will be difficult because of differences on spending and tax increases. The stock market dropped due to worries about continued disagreements.

In the Senate, Democrats kept their slim majority, gaining three seats and losing one. In the presidential election, Obama won many swing states, including Ohio and Virginia. Romney only won North Carolina.

In his victory speech, Obama asked for electoral reform because of long queues at voting stations. He also repeated his famous "hope" slogan from 2008. Romney conceded to Obama in a phone call and gave a gracious speech, saying that Americans need their leaders to work together.

The election was a test of Obama's presidency, which has been disappointing some supporters due to slow economic growth and high unemployment. Many Americans are relieved that he won and will continue as President.

Sweden is considered the best country for older people, while Afghanistan is the worst. However, having a lot of money doesn't always mean that older people will have better lives. This was found by the first global index on ageing.

The US is in eighth place despite being one of the richest countries in the world. The UK didn't make it into the top ten. Some surprising results include Sri Lanka ranking higher than Pakistan, and Bolivia and Mauritius doing well considering their economies.

Mark Gorman from HelpAge International said that history plays a big role in how well older people are treated. Countries like Sweden have made choices to support their older population through good education and healthcare. The index looked at 91 countries and found that over half of the world's older people live in poor countries.

By 2050, there will be two billion people aged 60 or over, which is more than one-fifth of the world's population. This demographic shift is happening fastest in developing countries. In some countries, like Jordan and Vietnam, the number of older people is expected to triple by 2050.

The index also found that women generally outlive men. Women often face disadvantages in old age due to lack of paid work, less decision-making power, and vulnerability to violence. However, if governments make the right decisions, population ageing doesn't necessarily mean higher healthcare spending.

Some countries have made good choices for their older populations. For example, Bolivia has introduced free health care and a non-contributory universal pension. Nepal also introduced a basic pension for people over 70 without other income.

Good education systems are important for older people to deal with bureaucracy. Chile and Costa Rica have good healthcare systems that benefit their ageing populations. Education is crucial for basic literacy, which helps older people navigate the system.

The ageing index was created using 13 indicators across four areas: income security, health care, employment and education, and an enabling environment. The creators of the index hope it will help governments understand the needs and opportunities of older people.

Clay Cockrell is a therapist who helps wealthy people in New York City. He understands their problems because he used to work on Wall Street and now spends his days walking with them in Central Park or Battery Park.

Cockrell says that the rich often feel guilty about having too much money, worried they will be judged by others, and isolated from the rest of society. They may even hide their wealth from friends and family.

This is not a new problem, but it has gotten worse since the financial crisis in 2008. The Occupy Wall Street movement highlighted income inequality, which made some people view the rich negatively.

Experts like Jamie Traeger-Muney and Barbara Nusbaum agree that being wealthy can be isolating. People with money often feel uncomfortable talking about their wealth and may hide it from others.

The gap between the rich and poor is growing worldwide. According to Oxfam, the richest 1% now own nearly half of global wealth, up from 44% in 2009. In the US, the top 0.1% households have seen their wealth increase from 7% to 22% over three decades.

Cockrell says that many of his wealthy clients struggle with trusting their friendships and feeling isolated from others. They may feel like they can't be themselves because of their wealth.

A study by the Gates Foundation found that being part of the 1% can be difficult, as people often judge you for your money rather than getting to know you as a person. Some wealthy individuals even keep their wealth secret due to fear of negative judgment.

Cockrell advises his clients not to let their money define them and to acknowledge their legitimate problems, just like anyone else.

Takahito Iguchi thinks Google Glasses are not cool. He believes people look silly wearing them, and Google made a mistake by giving the first 10,000 pairs to software developers instead of famous people like supermodels or Scarlett Johansson.

Iguchi wants to create a better version of Google Glass called Telepathy One. It's an augmented reality device that looks more stylish and Japanese. Iguchi is launching Telepathy One at the South by Southwest festival in Austin, Texas, and it has already attracted $5m in investment.

Telepathy One will be simpler than Google Glass. Instead of doing many things like browsing the internet or taking pictures, it will focus on communication. You can use it to share photos and videos with friends and family in real-time. Iguchi hopes this device will help people understand each other better.

Iguchi is a Japanese entrepreneur who has worked in the tech industry for 20 years. He believes that technology can bring people closer together and make them more understanding of others. He's not worried about competing with Google, which he sees as a mighty force. Instead, he thinks small companies like his own can sometimes be more successful.

Iguchi is building Telepathy One in Japan, but developing its applications will happen in the US. Some Japanese news crews are interested in him because he might be a new example of how Japanese entrepreneurs can succeed abroad.

Building the prototype of Telepathy One was easy, but presenting it to the world is harder. Iguchi thinks that companies like Apple have been successful by telling stories about their products and making them appealing to customers.

Iguchi hopes that Telepathy One will make people more understanding of each other by giving them access to information from social networks and the cloud. He believes that if we can see someone else's point of view, we'll be able to understand them better. As a student, Iguchi studied philosophy and taught himself how to code. He thinks that code is a way for humans to share information and connect with each other.

Iguchi wants Telepathy One to help people overcome their differences and end wars by making it easier for us to see and understand each other's perspectives.

Google's vice-president, Vint Cerf, has warned that many digital files created today may be lost forever because the programs needed to view them will become outdated. This is called "bit rot". Cerf thinks that if we don't take action, future historians will not be able to access important documents and information from our daily lives.

The problem is that software and hardware used in the past are no longer supported or available. For example, it's already difficult to play old computer games because the equipment needed to run them is now mostly found in museums.

Cerf suggests creating a system called "digital vellum" to preserve old software and hardware so that out-of-date files can still be accessed in the future. He also advises people to print out important photos and documents instead of just saving them digitally.

The issue highlights an irony: while we digitize things to preserve them, we may actually make them harder to access if we don't take steps to ensure their long-term survival. Cerf warns that important historical documents, such as emails and letters, may be lost forever because they can only be interpreted with dedicated software and hardware.

Researchers are working on a solution to this problem, but it's not just a matter of inventing new technology - it's also about navigating the legal permissions to copy and store software before it dies. Cerf thinks that we need to rethink our approach to copyright, patents, and licensing in order to preserve digital files for hundreds or even thousands of years.

Some examples of what might be lost include:

* Emails and letters from important historical figures
* Old computer games like Jet Set Willy and Doom
* Important political documents, such as the letters of Abraham Lincoln's team
* Digital versions of ancient civilizations' histories and cultures

Researchers at Carnegie Mellon University are making progress on a solution to bit rot by taking digital snapshots of computer hard drives while they run different software programs. This allows them to upload the files to a computer that can mimic the one the software ran on, making it possible to read otherwise defunct files.

Cerf suggests that people should take steps to preserve their own digital lives and important documents, such as printing out photos and letters, or using online services that specialize in preserving digital files.

A big day started with police raids on a hotel in Zurich. By the end, 16 football officials from around the world were charged with corruption in the US. These officials included five current or former members of FIFA's executive committee. 

They were accused of being part of kickback schemes that involved millions of dollars in bribes. The US Department of Justice said this was a big betrayal of trust and very unacceptable.

On the same day, Swiss police arrested two important football leaders: Juan Ángel Napout from South America and Alfredo Hawit from North and Central America. They had only taken their jobs recently after previous leaders were arrested.

The Swiss government said these men will be held in custody until they can be sent to the US to face charges. The US Attorney General, Loretta Lynch, said they are suspected of accepting millions of dollars in bribes.

So far, 11 current or former members of FIFA's executive committee have been charged with corruption. This includes eight people who have already pleaded guilty. The investigation claims that $200 million was given as bribes to football officials, mostly from TV and marketing contracts.

Loretta Lynch said that anyone involved in this corruption will be caught and brought to justice. Fourteen men were charged with corruption last May, but now 27 people are accused of being part of the scheme.

FIFA's acting president, Issa Hayatou, denied that FIFA was corrupt. He said only a few individuals were involved in this scandal. However, many people have been accused of corruption within FIFA over the past year.

The investigation is still ongoing and more charges may be made. The leaders of several regional football bodies, including CONCACAF and Conmebol, have all been charged with corruption.

How long can you hold your breath? I tried holding mine and found it got easier at first but then harder. After one minute and 12 seconds, I had to stop. Some people, like freedivers, need to hold their breath for a long time while swimming underwater.

I met a freediver named Sam Amps who could hold her breath for five minutes while swimming. She said she trained herself by breathing slowly before diving and resisting the urge to breathe for longer than usual. 

Some scientists think that humans may have evolved from water-dwelling animals because we can hold our breath for a bit. However, this idea is not supported by scientific evidence.

We're not unique in being able to hold our breath, as other mammals can do it too. When you're submerged in cold water, your heart rate slows down, but this isn't special to humans and happens with all air-breathing animals.

However, our ability to hold our breath is useful in medicine, especially when giving radiotherapy for breast cancer. If patients can stay still while holding their breath, the treatment is more effective. Doctors at University Hospital Birmingham have found that by ventilating patients with oxygen-rich air before a breath-hold, they can hold their breath for up to five-and-a-half minutes.

The key seems to be not just about fooling the body's sensors but also making the diaphragm muscle less tired. This is because when you breathe in and out, your diaphragm contracts and relaxes. When you're holding your breath, your diaphragm stays contracted until it eventually gets too tired and makes you breathe again.

In summary, while our ability to hold our breath isn't special, it can be useful in some situations, like giving radiotherapy for breast cancer.

The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge won a small victory in their fight for privacy when a French court stopped a magazine from publishing pictures of them taken at a private chateau. However, this is just the beginning of the case.

A French prosecutor will now decide if the magazine editor and photographer can be charged with a crime for taking pictures of the duchess sunbathing topless while on holiday in France. This could lead to up to one year in prison and a fine of €45,000.

The court ordered the magazine Closer to hand over digital copies of the pictures within 24 hours and pay €2,000 in legal costs. If they don't comply, they will face a fine of €10,000 per day. The couple did not ask for damages.

The judges said that taking pictures of someone at home, even if it's private property, is intrusive and can be considered a crime. They also ruled that every photograph published by the magazine in France in the future must carry a fine of €10,000.

However, this only applies to the 14 pictures already published. The magazine editor has hinted that there may be more intimate pictures. A spokesperson for the royal couple said they welcome the judge's decision and believe the law was broken.

The couple is taking further action by asking for a criminal prosecution against the magazine and photographer. This means the prosecutor will decide who to charge, but it's understood they want to charge the editor of Closer and whoever took the pictures.

French law allows for up to one year in prison and a fine of €45,000 for breach of privacy. The couple wants to set an example to deter paparazzi from taking intrusive photos in the future.

Their lawyers didn't ask for copies of the magazine to be removed from shelves, but several online stores took them down after complaints.

Galina Zaglumyonova woke up in her flat in Chelyabinsk when there was a huge explosion. She looked out the window and saw a big cloud in the sky and heard car alarms from the street below. She thought it might be a plane crash, but it was actually a 10-tonne meteorite falling to Earth.

The meteorite broke into pieces as it entered the atmosphere at a speed of over 33,000 miles per hour. It caused panic in Chelyabinsk, where more than 1 million people live. Many people were injured by flying glass, and some buildings were damaged.

A team from the Russian Academy of Sciences said that the meteorite broke up into pieces between 18 and 32 miles above the ground. The vapour trail from the meteorite was visible for hundreds of miles around.

Many schools and universities in Chelyabinsk closed after the incident. Some people were injured, including children. Tatyana Bets, a nurse at a hospital clinic, said that she saw many students who were frightened and shocked.

The damage caused by the meteorite is estimated to be over 1 billion roubles (around £20 million). The government has started cleaning up the area.

Some people thought that the meteorite might have been shot down by Russian air defence units. However, experts say this is unlikely. They also ruled out any connection with a nearby asteroid called 2012 DA14.

The leader of Russia's Liberal Democrat party, Vladimir Zhirinovsky, said that it was not a meteorite but an American test of new weapons. Some people are trying to sell pieces of the meteorite on the internet.

President Putin and Prime Minister Medvedev were informed about the incident. Medvedev said that it shows how vulnerable our planet is. Russia's Deputy Prime Minister, Dmitry Rogozin, called for a warning system to be created to detect objects from space.

Glastonbury Festival wants to reduce plastic waste. Every year, people throw away one million plastic water bottles on the site. The festival is trying to stop this by giving out reusable stainless-steel bottles to staff and selling them to visitors. 

The organizers also want everyone to bring their own refillable bottle to fill with water at 400 special taps across the site. They want to encourage people to use tap water instead of bottled water, which can harm the environment.

Lucy Smith, who is in charge of making Glastonbury more environmentally friendly, said: "We have good water quality in the UK, but everyone likes drinking bottled water." 

Glastonbury wants to be the most eco-friendly music festival in the world. They plan to make all their beer glasses and cutlery reusable next year.

Did you know that plastic waste can take hundreds or even thousands of years to break down? Also, making plastic bottles uses a lot of oil and produces carbon emissions when water is transported around the world.

Every year, 13 billion plastic water bottles are sold in the UK, but only one in five is recycled. The festival wants visitors to use tap water instead of bottled water and to take their rubbish home with them.

To help people, WaterAid will set up special kiosks where you can get free refills of water from reusable bottles. 

The festival organizers are trying hard to reduce waste. They say that last year, half of all the rubbish left on site was recycled. This year, there will be 15,000 bins for recycling.

Some people criticize Glastonbury for becoming too commercial, but the festival is still committed to being eco-friendly.

Stratford-upon-Avon wants to celebrate William Shakespeare in 2016 as their famous man from Avon. Born in Warwickshire in 1564, he died there 400 years ago. Stratford remained important throughout his life, says Paul Edmondson, head of the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust.

Many people think Shakespeare ignored Stratford and only went back to die, but he actually bought land and property there, kept a library, and lived and read in the town. This year, Stratford will remind everyone of its importance to Shakespeare's life.

The anniversary of his death will be marked across Britain and the world with theatre performances, lectures, exhibitions, and more. Macbeth will open in Singapore, Romeo and Juliet in Brussels, and a 37-screen pop-up cinema will show all of Shakespeare's plays along London's South Bank.

There is little evidence about Shakespeare's life, but his friends saved his plays by gathering drafts, scripts, and other papers into the First Folio, published seven years after he died. The actor Mark Rylance loves this book, and some of the surviving copies will be on display in London.

An exhibition at Somerset House will show important documents, including Shakespeare's will and signatures. Stratford-upon-Avon claims to have made and educated Shakespeare, but Paul Edmondson says he was born there and bought a house where he died.

Shakespeare's old school room is being restored with a £1.4m grant and will open as a visitor attraction. His former home, New Place, was the second-best house in Stratford, and he probably wrote some of his late plays there. However, the house was demolished 300 years ago, and only its foundations remain.

A five-year archaeology project has uncovered Shakespeare's kitchen in the cellars, and the site is being redisplayed for the anniversary. Without Stratford, Edmondson says, there would have been no Shakespeare.

One day in August, one in seven people on Earth, which is about 1 billion people, used Facebook according to Mark Zuckerberg. In ten years, Facebook changed many things in our lives.

Mark Zuckerberg said "A more open and connected world is a better world." It brought stronger relationships with the people we love, a stronger economy with more opportunities, and a stronger society that shares all of our values.

Facebook has changed how we use some words. Now we can say "unfriend" someone easily on Facebook. But in real life, ending a friendship can be very painful. Facebook also changes how we see our friends. We have many online friends, but we may not really know them well. 

Professor Robin Dunbar said that people can only have about 150 close relationships. He thinks Facebook makes it too easy to end friendships, so we might stop learning to get along with others.

Many people on Facebook don't care as much about their private information. They share a lot of details like photos and where they live. Brands use this information to target them with ads.

Facebook has created many jobs in the advertising industry. Marketers can understand their customers better than ever before because of the data available on Facebook.

However, Facebook also makes it easy for people to complain about brands online. This can make problems go viral quickly.

Facebook has been used to organize revolutions and protests around the world. In Ukraine, Facebook was a key tool for organizing the Euromaidan protests. Many people relied on Facebook for news and information during these events.

Nowadays, many people get their news from Facebook or other social media. Facebook makes it easy for news companies to sell ads and reach more people. This has changed how journalists write stories and how they find information.

In the past, Facebook was mainly used by students at elite universities in the US. But now, 56% of internet users aged 65 and over have a Facebook account. People are using groups and pages on Facebook differently too. They're sharing more photos and videos instantly from their mobile phones.

Some people think that Facebook might not be around forever, but it will likely continue to change and stay a major player in the world of social media.

**Climate Change Will Affect Poor Countries Hardest**

Over the next 100 years, poor countries will face big changes in the weather. This is because of human activities that release bad things into the air and make the Earth's temperature rise.

The United Nations (UN) has looked at this problem carefully and says:

* The sea level will rise slowly.
* Cyclones (strong winds and rainstorms) will be stronger.
* It will get hotter during the day and night.
* Rainfall will become more unpredictable.
* Heatwaves (very hot weather) will last longer.

In East Africa, there will be more short rains. In West Africa, there will be heavier monsoons (big rainfalls). In countries like Bangladesh, India, and Burma, cyclones will be stronger.

The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) report says that some areas will get more rainfall, but many dry areas will get less. This means that:

* Monsoon seasons might start earlier or stay longer.
* Extreme rain events will happen more often in tropical regions.

Scientists from poor countries have welcomed the report and say it confirms what they already know: climate change is real and happening fast.

**Important Facts**

* Sea levels are expected to rise by 40-62 cm (15.7-24.4 inches) by 2100.
* Many cities in developing countries, like Lagos and Calcutta, are at risk due to rising sea levels.
* Weather disasters will be more likely in a warmer world.
* Crop production and incomes might decrease, making people hungrier.

**What Can Be Done?**

The report says that we need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to slow down climate change. We also need to help poor countries adapt to the changes they are already facing.

There's a time in many people's lives when things seem less happy. Some men buy expensive cars or make big changes to their lifestyle during this time. This is called a midlife crisis. But is it just for humans? 

A team of scientists from around the world has studied chimpanzees and orangutans at zoos. They asked carers who work with these animals about how they feel. The scientists found that these apes also have a period when their happiness decreases, like middle-aged men. This happens in their 20s and 30s.

The researchers asked zookeepers to complete questionnaires about the animals' mood, social behavior, and goals. Over 500 apes from various zoos were included in the study. The results showed that well-being decreased for the chimpanzees at around 28-29 years old and for orangutans at 35-36 years old.

A scientist from Edinburgh University said this could be because of age-related changes in the brain, similar to humans. Another expert suggested it might be due to watching other apes get sick or die. However, some experts are skeptical about these findings.

They question why middle-aged animals would experience a decline in happiness like humans do. One expert pointed out that animals don't think ahead and plan for the future like humans do. 

Despite this, one of the researchers believes their study could help us understand more about what causes midlife crisis in some men. He suggests looking at what's similar between middle-aged humans, chimps, and orangutans to find answers.

Important note: The study found a decline in well-being among middle-aged chimpanzees and orangutans, which may be related to age-related changes in the brain or watching other apes get sick/die. However, some experts are skeptical about these findings.

Do you think of Amazon as a big forest, a long river, or the biggest online shop? Actually, there's a debate about what Amazon really means. Brazil and Peru are objecting to an American company's plan to use ".amazon" as its internet address. They think this will stop people using it for important things like protecting the environment and helping indigenous communities.

The US company wants to use ".amazon" because it's its brand name, but the South American governments say this is not fair. They want to keep the internet address free for public use.

This debate is about how the internet should be organized. Until now, there were only a few types of internet addresses like ".com", ".gov", and ".org". But soon there will be many more, and some countries are worried that companies will get the good names and people won't be able to use them for important things.

Amazon has applied for many new internet addresses, including ".shop" and ".book", but its plan for ".amazon" is causing problems. Brazil and Peru have asked ICANN (the organization in charge of the internet) to reject Amazon's application. They think a private company shouldn't get a name that refers to an important area like the Amazon rainforest.

Other countries are also objecting to certain names, like ".patagonia", which is claimed by an American outdoor clothing company, and ".shangrila", which is proposed by a hotel group in China. The authorities in Beijing say the name "Shangri-La" actually belongs to a region in Yunnan province.

The organization in charge of the internet, ICANN, has recommended that disputed proposals be put on hold until July. They will discuss them again then and decide what to do.

Joseph Roche is a scientist who has doubts about Mars One, a private project that wants to send humans to live on Mars from 2025. He's different from other critics because he was chosen as one of the top candidates for the mission.

Roche works at Trinity College in Dublin and wrote an article in The Guardian expressing his concerns. He says the selection process wasn't good enough and that the team running Mars One is too optimistic about their chances. They think they can do it alone, but Roche believes they should work with other scientists to make it happen.

Roche also criticized how Mars One announced its top candidates. They ranked them based on how many supporters they had, not on their qualifications or skills. The rankings didn't mean the top candidates were the best ones; instead, it showed who had donated more money to the project.

Mars One's plan is ambitious: they want to send a lander and satellite to Mars in 2018, followed by a rover in 2020 and cargo missions starting in 2022. Humans would start arriving in 2025 and stay on Mars permanently. However, another scientist, Gerard't Hooft, who supports the project, thinks this timeline is too optimistic.

Roche spoke to Medium, a US blogging platform that also has doubts about Mars One. He revealed that only 2,761 people applied to be astronauts, not 200,000 as claimed by Mars One. Roche had a disappointing experience with the selection process; he was asked to sign a non-disclosure agreement before being interviewed and then had a short Skype call instead of a longer interview.

Roche doesn't want to give more interviews because he's worried about speaking negatively about space travel. However, he believes that Mars One should be more open and transparent about their plans and timelines.

Roche is passionate about space exploration and thinks it's great that Mars One has sparked interesting discussions about the ethics and morality of future missions. However, he doesn't think a one-way mission to Mars will happen in his lifetime.

A small room in Dhaka's slums looks like a classroom, but it's not easy for children to learn there. The walls are made of corrugated iron, and the air is full of chemicals that hurt people's eyes and throats. However, this is better than working in nearby factories.

For 14 years, an organization called SOHAY has been helping child laborers go to school. They have set up 23 centers in Dhaka where children can learn and do their homework with the help of their friends. Alamin, a 10-year-old boy who used to work in a plastic factory, now attends one of these centers.

SOHAY's goal is to make education more accessible for children living in slums. Their program manager, Mohammed Abdullah al-Mamun, says that it's challenging to get child laborers into school because they often struggle to make friends and adapt to the classroom environment. The dropout rate is high, but SOHAY works with schools to help them understand the needs of these children.

Seven-year-old Zhorna Akter Sumayya used to live in a slum where her brothers worked long hours. But after being introduced to education at one of SOHAY's centers, she now goes to a state primary school. SOHAY has helped many children leave hazardous work and enter school. In 2015, they helped 1,540 children leave work and 2,125 vulnerable children enter school.

Bangladesh's Labor Law bans children under 14 from working, but many are still employed in informal sectors or hazardous industries. According to UNICEF, 4.7 million children under the age of 14 work in informal sectors, and 1.3 million aged five to 17 work in hazardous industries.

Another organization, Sonjag, has also been working with communities in Dhaka's slums to get children into school. They talk to community members about the importance of education and work closely with volunteers and social workers to motivate employers to let children leave for school.

A senior US researcher, Kurt Fristrup, is warning that people today may lose the ability to hear and appreciate the sounds of nature. This could be a problem because it's good for our health and well-being to listen to natural sounds like birdsong and running water.

Fristrup says that people are listening to music through their headphones instead of paying attention to the sounds around them. He calls this "learned deafness" and says it's a real issue. We are training ourselves to ignore the information our ears receive, which is not good for us.

The US National Park Service has been measuring sound levels in many places across the US over the past 10 years. They found that almost all areas were affected by noise from human activity like cars and planes. Fristrup's team created a model of noise levels across the US and predicts that noise pollution is growing faster than the population.

Noise pollution can have negative effects on our hearing and make us less able to appreciate the sounds around us. Even in cities, there are often birds and other natural sounds worth listening to, but these may be lost if we continue to ignore them.

Some scientists believe that listening to natural sounds can be beneficial for our health. Derrick Taff reported on an experiment where people who listened to recordings of nature sounds after a stressful event recovered faster than those who listened to urban sounds like traffic and planes.

Fristrup thinks that over time, we may forget how quiet the world used to be and accept noise pollution as normal. He fears that many children will grow up without experiencing peace and quiet in their environment.

Taff recommends listening to nature recordings to help calm down and appreciate the natural world. Fristrup suggests that we go back to listening to our surroundings and appreciating the sounds of nature, rather than ignoring them through headphones or earbuds.

Here are the six jobs simplified to B1 reading level:

**1. Race Engineer**

A race engineer works between the driver and mechanics in a racing team. They help drivers improve their car's performance by analyzing data and making decisions about the car's setup. To be successful, you need to work well under pressure.

Salary: £25,000-£90,000 per year

Qualifications: University degree in automotive or mechanical engineering

**2. Ethical Hacker**

An ethical hacker tests computer systems to see if they are secure. They try to find weaknesses and fix them before hackers can use them for bad things. You don't need a computer science degree, but you do need analytical skills and attention to detail.

Salary: £35,000-£90,000 per year

Qualifications: Wide range of qualifications accepted

**3. Bomb-Disposal Diver**

A bomb-disposal diver searches for unexploded bombs underwater and disposes of them safely. You need special diving and medical training, as well as experience handling explosives.

Salary: Up to £100,000 per year (part-time)

Qualifications: Diving-inspection and medical-technician qualifications

**4. Social Engineer**

A social engineer tries to trick people into giving away company secrets or accessing secure information. You need strong communication skills, a background in IT, and a good understanding of psychology.

Salary: £50,000-£80,000 per year

Qualifications: Degree in IT or related field

**5. Power-Line Helicopter Pilot**

A power-line helicopter pilot flies close to high-voltage power lines to inspect them with a camera. You need special flying training and experience.

Salary: £65,000 per year

Qualifications: Private-helicopter-pilot licence and commercial pilot's licence

**6. Private Butler**

A private butler takes care of the daily needs of their employer, including managing staff, serving meals, and running errands. You don't need specific qualifications, but a course in butling can be helpful.

Salary: £60,000-£90,000 per year

Qualifications: Course at the British Butler Academy or similar institution

India's wealthy people are expected to become even richer by 2018. According to a report, the country's richest individuals will have four times more money than they do now. This growth comes despite recent problems such as slow economic growth, high food prices, and a weak currency.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won an election in 2014 with promises to improve the economy. Even though there was a slowdown, India's rich people are still doing well. There are almost six more Indians who have over $3.75 million than there were three years ago.

India's wealthy individuals hold assets worth one trillion dollars, which is about one-fifth of the country's total wealth. By 2018, this number could increase to four trillion dollars, making many more people multimillionaires.

A growing luxury market in India serves the new and old rich people. They want to show off their wealth discreetly, so they buy luxury goods like cars, designer clothes, and jewelry. Cars are popular items to buy, with foreign brands becoming increasingly desirable.

However, India's poor infrastructure restricts demand for high-end products. The country's super-rich have a reputation for spending extravagantly, with examples including a billionaire's $1 billion home in Mumbai and a tycoon's niece's $80 million wedding in Barcelona.

Luxury goods buyers are becoming more demanding, seeking exclusive experiences that no one else can replicate. Some buy expensive items just to show off their wealth, while others donate large amounts of money to charity. Despite the growth of the wealthy class, India's social norms accept a wide gap between rich and poor people.

Key statistics:

* India's richest individuals will have four times more money by 2018
* There are almost six more Indians with over $3.75 million than three years ago
* India's wealthy individuals hold assets worth one trillion dollars
* By 2018, this number could increase to four trillion dollars
* Almost half of new ultra-high-net-worth individuals live in smaller cities
