Margaret Thatcher, the most powerful British prime minister since Winston Churchill in 1940, has died. She was a strong supporter of free market economics and had a significant impact on global politics. The British government said she will have a ceremonial funeral with military honors at St Paul's Cathedral.

The current prime minister, David Cameron, said he is sad about her death. He remembered Thatcher as a great leader who "saved" Britain and called her the greatest peacetime prime minister in British history.

US President Barack Obama also paid tribute to Thatcher. He said she stood up for what she believed in and showed that people can shape their own destiny with courage and determination.

Margaret Thatcher was the first woman to lead a major Western country and served as prime minister for 11 years. She had been ill with dementia and suffered from mini-strokes in 2002, which led her to step down from public life.

People across different political parties have paid tribute to Thatcher. Labour leader Ed Miliband said she was a unique figure who changed British politics and had a big impact on the world stage. Deputy prime minister Nick Clegg called her one of the most important figures in modern British politics.

Thatcher's time as prime minister was marked by significant events, including her close relationship with US President Ronald Reagan during the Cold War. She also introduced market reforms at home, which led to denationalization and privatization of state-owned industries. However, this also led to conflicts with trade unions and some members of her own party.

Thatcher's legacy is complex, but she remains a significant figure in British history. She was known for her strong personality and her ability to shape global politics.

Here's the simplified text at B1 (intermediate) reading level:

Every day, students at St Ninian's Primary School in Stirling run a mile around their school field. This has been happening for three-and-a-half years and it seems to be working very well. Most of the children are not overweight, unlike many other kids in the UK.

The daily mile has helped these children become fitter, behave better, and focus more in class. Many schools across Britain have started doing this too. They take 15 minutes during the day for their students to run or walk around the school or a nearby park.

Elaine Wyllie, the headteacher of St Ninian's, is very proud of what they've achieved. "It's amazing that children all over the country are starting to run every day because of something we've done," she said.

According to official figures, one in ten children is obese when they start school at age four or five. A study found that English schoolchildren were the least fit ever recorded in 2015. So, many primary schools have started introducing the daily mile to improve their students' fitness levels.

Elaine Wyllie says it's a simple and fun way for kids to exercise. "They come back into class looking happy and healthy," she said. Teachers take their students out of lessons to run around the school field whenever it fits with their schedule. Only bad weather stops them from doing it.

Researchers from Stirling University are studying the benefits of the daily mile to see if it really makes a difference. They will compare the students at St Ninian's with kids from another school in Stirling that hasn't started this program yet.

Other schools and organizations are also interested in starting the daily mile. A group of experts from Cheshire is visiting Scotland to learn more about it. If they see good results, they might introduce it in all 450 schools in their region. Paralympian Tanni Grey-Thompson thinks that's a great idea. "All children need at least 60 minutes of exercise every day," she said.

The Scottish government supports the daily mile too. They think it's a good way to encourage kids and parents to be more active and healthy.

Canadian tennis player Frank Dancevic was very unhappy with the Australian Open organizers because they made players compete in very hot conditions. He collapsed on court after temperatures rose to 41C (106F). 

Dancevic said it was unfair to make players compete in such heat. He also said that he started hallucinating and saw Snoopy, a character from a cartoon. "I was dizzy from the middle of the first set," he explained. "Then I thought I saw Snoopy and it seemed weird." 

Other players agreed with Dancevic. The British number one tennis player, Andy Murray, said: "It's not good when people are collapsing. We have to think about our safety." Caroline Wozniacki mentioned that her water bottle started melting on the court, which shows how hot it was. John Isner compared the heat to an oven. 

The defending champion, Victoria Azarenka, said it felt like dancing in a frying pan. The tournament organizers tried to help players by giving them extra time to rest between sets. However, they did not stop the matches because of the heat.

Dancevic continued playing after medical attention but lost his match. He was not running much towards the end and just felt very hot. A ball boy also collapsed during a match, which made organizers shorten their work shifts.

Some officials said that only a few players experienced health problems, but others were more concerned about the risks of heat-related illness. Roger Federer thought it was a mental issue for players, but Dancevic disagreed. He said some players are naturally better at handling heat and others are not.

Dancevic also mentioned that he still couldn't pee after his match, which shows how dehydrated he was.

Sir Alex Ferguson is leaving his job as manager of Manchester United at the end of the season after 27 years. This makes him the most successful manager in British football history. He has won many titles, including 13 Premier League championships, two Champions Leagues, and five FA Cups.

Ferguson said he thought a lot about his decision to retire and believes it is the right time. He wants to leave Manchester United in good shape for the future. The team's quality and youth set-up will help them succeed in the long term, and their training facilities are among the best in the world.

As part of his retirement plan, Ferguson will become a director and ambassador for the club. He thanked his family, players, and staff for their support over the years. His wife, Cathy, has been very important to him throughout his career.

Ferguson also thanked the Glazer family, who own Manchester United, for giving him the chance to manage the team. He worked closely with chief executive David Gill, who is retiring too. The two men have a good relationship and have planned for Ferguson's retirement together.

The players were told about Ferguson's decision in an emotional meeting on Wednesday morning. René Meulensteen, one of the coaches, said he was surprised but not shocked by the news.

Joel Glazer, a joint owner of Manchester United, praised Ferguson as a fantastic manager and wonderful person. His brother Avie Glazer is also pleased that Ferguson will stay with the club as a director. David Gill said working with Ferguson has been an incredible experience and that he will never forget what he has done for the club.

Ferguson's legacy at Manchester United will not be forgotten, and his successor will have a good team to work with. The fans are being thanked for their support over the years, which has meant a lot to him.

Lego's profits increased significantly in the first half of 2014 due to the success of their movie, The Lego Movie. This film was popular in the US and UK, making over $250 million in the US and £31 million in the UK by April. 

The movie was made for about $60 million and is considered a great example of successful marketing. It created entertaining content that appealed to people who would buy Lego products. 

Lego's finance director said that the success of The Lego Movie helped their sales, which rose 11% during this time. Operating profit increased by 12%, reaching $630 million.

Their CEO, Jørgen Vig Knudstorp, said that this result is a good sign of Lego's growth in recent years, despite the tough economic environment. He believes it's because they can develop and sell successful products, like their famous bricks, which children love around the world.

Lego was founded in 1949 in a small town called Billund. By the 1970s, they were a well-known toy brand globally. However, they had some financial problems and were close to going bankrupt in 2003. Their new CEO made changes to help the company recover. 

In April, Lego opened their first factory in China and an office in Shanghai to expand into this important market.

Here's a simplified version of the text at B1 (intermediate) reading level:

A wealthy Chinese businessman named Gao Ping lived in Spain. He owned many luxury items, including expensive cars and art. However, he didn't have much money in his bank account, which made Spanish authorities suspicious.

Gao had a lot of power because he controlled the supplies to 4,000 bazaars across Spain. But, police suspected that he wasn't paying taxes on the goods he was importing from China.

In 2012, police found €12 million in cash at Gao's warehouses. They accused him and his gang of laundering up to €300 million a year by selling counterfeit goods and hiding money. The government said this was hurting Spain's economy.

The €500 note is a big problem because it's easy to transport and hide. Some people use it for tax evasion, money laundering, and terrorism. In 2010, the UK stopped using these notes because they were mainly used by criminals.

Many experts think that high-value notes like the €500 should be abolished. Peter Sands, a former bank head, said that they make it easy for "bad guys" to hide their money. Even if criminals find ways to use smaller bills or other materials, these would be bulkier and easier to track.

The European Central Bank (ECB) has been asked to look at whether to continue printing the €500 note. The head of Europol, Rob Wainwright, said that it makes it easy for terrorists to hide their money.

Some countries like Germany and Austria prefer using cash because it's cheap and accepted everywhere. However, law enforcement officials are concerned about people hiding large amounts of cash.

In one case, two men tried to deposit €200,000 in torn and muddy €500 notes into a bank. In another case, €1.3 million was found hidden in a suitcase.

Europol wants central banks to take responsibility for the strange uses of the €500 note. They want them to explain why so many high-value notes are being printed, especially by countries like Luxembourg that don't use much cash.

The European Central Bank's head, Mario Draghi, has said he doesn't want the income from printing the notes to help criminals. Some other officials think there is no evidence linking the €500 note to crime, but this argument may not be enough anymore.

EU finance ministers have asked policymakers to explore restrictions on high-value notes and report back by 2016.

McDonald's is facing big problems around the world. It's no longer the popular fast-food chain it used to be. In 2013, its worldwide sales dropped by 3.3%. This is a big problem because McDonald's has been expanding for 10 years.

In some places, like China and Europe, people are not buying as much from McDonald's as they used to. There was a food scare in China where workers were caught on camera saying they use old beef and chicken in McDonald's products. In Russia, many of McDonald's restaurants are being investigated by health inspectors for possible food safety problems.

The biggest problem is in the US, where McDonald's has about 40% of its restaurants. For the last year, sales have been going down there too. Young people are not eating at McDonald's as much anymore because they prefer to go to other places like Chipotle Mexican Grill. In fact, a poll of over 32,000 American diners found that McDonald's hamburgers were considered the worst in America.

People are also concerned about the healthiness of McDonald's food. Many believe it is not healthy and prefers to eat at places like Chipotle, which offers antibiotic-free meat and locally sourced produce. McDonald's has even started a website where customers can ask questions about its food, but some of the answers have raised more doubts.

McDonald's Chief Executive Don Thompson said the company needs to do a better job explaining how fresh and healthy its ingredients are. However, the company is also facing problems with slow service and high prices. Many consumers think McDonald's has become too expensive, especially since it introduced $2 items on its dollar menu.

In some countries like the UK, however, McDonald's has managed to turn things around by introducing a competitive breakfast menu, improving coffee, and offering free wi-fi. Executives are promising to address concerns about food quality in the US market.

Analysts are skeptical about how McDonald's can balance simpler menus with greater choice over fillings. The company is testing "build your own burger" at some locations but it's not clear if this will be successful. Despite declining sales, McDonald's plans to open 1,400 new restaurants globally by the end of 2014.

Some analysts think McDonald's market share will continue to shrink but they also warn against writing off the company. They predict that McDonald's will remain the number one fast-food chain in terms of total sales for years and decades to come.

We are close to a world where drones deliver packages. Amazon thinks this will happen soon, but others have concerns about safety.

Amazon's vice-president, Paul Misener, says his company is ready when regulations are in place. However, these rules won't be made until June 2016. Until then, drone technology has a long way to go. Only small drones weighing up to 25kg will be allowed. The Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) requires that all drones use different radio frequencies so they don't interfere with each other.

Professor Sajiv Singh from Carnegie Mellon University thinks piloting a drone is like leaving breadcrumbs for it to follow. However, even short flights have problems, such as finding hazards on the way and detecting obstacles. The vehicle needs to know where it is and how to avoid crashing.

Daniel Huber, a roboticist, says that losing contact with a drone is a major problem. If this happens, the drone will keep flying until it crashes. However, engineers are working on fixing this issue.

Jay McConville from Lockheed Martin says that drones have limitations, especially when it comes to size. A 25kg aircraft can't do everything. He wants drone piloting interfaces to be simpler and more focused on the end result, not every detail about the aircraft.

Daniel Huber is developing a program that uses drones to inspect infrastructure, such as pipelines and bridges. His algorithm allows a drone to fly around an area and report back with images.

Huber thinks that Amazon's plan to deliver packages using drones could work if they use vehicles that can stay in the air for 15 minutes and travel short distances. This would help keep people safe.

However, safety remains a major concern. Drones need to be able to detect hazards and avoid crashing. Singh points out that commercial aircraft have a much lower rate of failure than drones. The Reaper drone, for example, has one failure in 10,000 hours.

Singh thinks we're getting closer to making drones safe, but it's still a challenge. Part of the solution is contingency planning: if something goes wrong, the vehicle needs to do something reasonable.

Waiters at PizzaExpress are angry and want people's help. They're protesting because the company takes 8p from every £1 they earn in tips when customers pay with credit or debit cards. This means that workers, who already get paid the minimum wage of £6.50 an hour, lose a significant amount of money.

The protesters started an online petition and plan to demonstrate at PizzaExpress restaurants across the UK. They're also going to ask customers about the issue. According to Unite, the union organizing the protests, the company makes around £1 million a year from this practice.

One waiter who wants to remain anonymous said she loses £3 per night due to the deduction. She's been working at PizzaExpress for 15 years and relies heavily on tips to make ends meet. "I work hard and am good at my job," she wrote in a letter to Unite, "but when PizzaExpress takes a percentage of our tips, I get upset."

Other restaurant chains also take a percentage of workers' tips, but some deduct even more than PizzaExpress does. Ask and Zizzi take 8%, while Café Rouge, Bella Italia, Belgo, Strada, and Giraffe take 10%. On the other hand, Wagamama, Pizza Hut, and TGI Friday do not take any money from workers' tips.

The company says it uses the deducted amount to cover the cost of its "tronc" system, which is a way of distributing tips among staff. However, this explanation doesn't seem to satisfy the protesters or their supporters. Many people are signing an online petition against PizzaExpress's practice and some politicians are also getting involved.

Conservative MP Andrew Percy has promised to raise the issue in parliament after the summer recess. He wants to change the law so that restaurant staff have more control over their tips.

The National Security Agency (NSA) has access to the systems of big US internet companies like Google, Facebook, Apple, and others. This was revealed in a top-secret document that showed how the NSA can collect information such as search history, emails, file transfers, and live chats from these companies.

The document, called PRISM, says that the NSA can collect this information directly from the servers of these companies without needing their permission. However, when asked about this, all the companies denied any knowledge of PRISM or a similar program.

A Google spokesperson said: "We care deeply about the security of our users' data and only share it with the government if we have to."

The NSA access was made possible by changes in US surveillance law that were introduced under President Bush and renewed under President Obama in 2012. This law allows the NSA to collect information from anyone who uses the services of these companies, including people living outside the US or Americans who communicate with people outside the US.

This revelation is part of a bigger debate about how much the intelligence services are able to spy on people's online communications. Unlike previous leaks, this one shows that the NSA can actually read the content of emails and messages, not just look at who sent them to whom.

Some of the biggest internet companies in the world have been involved in PRISM since 2007, including Microsoft, Yahoo, Google, Facebook, PalTalk, YouTube, Skype, AOL, and Apple. The program is still growing and includes many other providers.

The NSA says that it only targets people living outside the US or Americans who communicate with people outside the US. However, critics argue that this law allows the NSA to collect information from anyone without needing a court order.

A chart prepared by the NSA shows the types of data it can collect, including email, video and voice chats, videos, photos, file transfers, and social networking details.

This leak is rare because the NSA is known for keeping secrets. However, a senior administration official said that the program is subject to oversight by several groups, including Congress, and that information collected under this program is used to protect the US from threats.

Do you want your child to be good at sports? Maybe they'll even make it to the Olympics or World Cup. Research suggests that children born in November or October are fitter and stronger than others in their class.

A study looked at 8,550 boys and girls aged between ten and sixteen from twenty-six schools in Essex. They were tested on three things: how long they could run without getting tired (stamina), how strong their hands were, and how powerful their legs were.

The results showed that children born in November were the fittest overall, followed closely by those born in October. Children born in December came close behind. However, some children in the same class who were born at different times of the year could have a big difference in physical ability.

For example, a boy born in November might be able to run 10% faster and jump 12% higher than a boy of the same age born in April. This is a big advantage in sports.

The study found that children born in April were the least fit, followed by those born in June. This could mean they have less chance of making it onto school teams or being good at sports.

Researchers think that children born in autumn might be healthier because their mothers got more vitamin D during pregnancy. Vitamin D is important for our health and wellbeing.

Experts say that how well a child does in PE and sports also depends on the quality of their introduction to these activities at school. If they have a positive experience, they are more likely to enjoy physical activity and do well in sports as they get older.

However, UK Sport says that while there might be some differences between children born in different months, it's not clear if this affects whether someone becomes an elite athlete or not. There are many factors that go into making a champion.

Here's the simplified text at a B1 reading level:

Kate Bush, a famous singer, recently performed live at the Hammersmith Apollo in London. Thirty-five years ago, when she first started performing, mobile phones were still being tested. Now, most people use their phones to watch and record concerts. Kate Bush is asking her fans to stop filming and taking photos during her shows.

On her website, Bush wrote: "I want to have a special connection with you as an audience, not through your screens. Please don't take pictures or videos." She chose a small theater for her concert series because she wants it to be an intimate experience. Bush is worried that if people record the show, they won't enjoy it fully and might even ruin it for others.

Other artists have also spoken out against phone use at concerts. Roger Daltrey from The Who thinks it's weird when people watch a show through their screens instead of paying attention to the music. Beyoncé once told a fan who was filming her concert: "Put that camera down! You're missing the moment!"

The debate about phone use at live events is not just limited to music. Fans in sports, like soccer and football, are also complaining about people using their phones during games. Some fans even protested against Wi-Fi being introduced at a stadium because they wanted to focus on the game.

Jarvis Cocker, Johnny Marr, and other artists have criticized phone-wielding audience members for missing out on the experience of live music. They think it's better to enjoy the show without distractions like phones.

However, some people disagree with these artists. A company that helps fans record concerts using their phones thinks that filming can actually enhance the experience. They create a video from all the footage taken by the audience, which makes for a unique and exciting memory of the concert.

Kate Bush's request to her fans is not new. Many artists have tried to ask people to put away their phones during live performances. Some even had to resort to putting up signs asking fans to be considerate. But some artists still think that fighting against phone use at concerts is a lost cause and that it's better to accept that filming is now part of the concert experience.

Leading water scientists have warned that the world's food supply may run out by 2050 if we don't make big changes. They say that people will need to eat more vegetarian food, like fruits and vegetables, and less meat.

Right now, about 20% of our protein comes from animal-based foods like meat and dairy products. But the scientists think this should drop to just 5%. This is because there won't be enough water to grow food for the expected 9 billion people by 2050 if we keep eating like we do now.

The report says that even with a vegetarian diet, there will still be problems with food shortages. This is why Oxfam and the UN are warning of another global food crisis in five years. Prices for basic foods like corn and wheat have already risen by nearly 50% due to droughts and poor rainfall.

A third of the world's arable land is used just to grow crops to feed animals, not people. To solve this problem, we need to be more careful with how we use water and food.

The scientists say that one option is for people to adopt a vegetarian diet. This can help increase the amount of water available to grow more food. Another option is to reduce waste and trade food between countries.

It's estimated that 900 million people already don't have enough to eat, and two billion are malnourished despite having enough food produced globally. The report says that growing more food will put even more pressure on the world's water resources.

The scientists are warning that competition for water between food production and other uses will become even more intense in the future. This is because the UN predicts we need to increase food production by 70% by mid-century, while also meeting rising energy demands.

A separate report suggests that helping farmers invest in simple technology like small pumps can help protect them from food insecurity in Africa and Asia. This could lead to big increases in yields and income for these farmers.

Key points:

* Water scientists warn of a global food shortage by 2050 if we don't change our eating habits.
* People may need to eat more vegetarian food to save water.
* Prices for basic foods have already risen by nearly 50% due to droughts and poor rainfall.
* One-third of the world's arable land is used just to grow crops to feed animals.
* Helping farmers invest in simple technology can protect them from food insecurity.
* We need to be more careful with how we use water and food.

Kiruna, a city in northern Sweden, needs to move because a huge iron-ore mine is eating away at its ground. The city has 23,000 people and was founded by the state-owned mining company LK in 1900. Kiruna's wealth comes from the big seam of iron ore beneath it.

However, the mine is now causing problems for the town. It's digging too close to the city, which will lead to buildings cracking and collapsing. This has been a problem for ten years, and people have put their lives on hold because they don't know what will happen.

The mining company wants to stop digging, but that would mean a lot of people losing their jobs. The city has decided to move instead. By 2033, the whole town will be relocated about 3 kilometers eastwards along a new high street. 

The architects in charge of the project call it a "dystopian choice." They have made a plan to rebuild the town with a higher-density arrangement of multi-storey apartment blocks and shared courtyards. A new town square is already being built, and some important buildings will be moved piece by piece.

However, not everything can be saved. Some people are worried about what they will lose when the city moves. They want to know how their homes will be valued and where they will live in the new town.

The mining company has agreed to pay for new facilities like schools and community centers, but many residents are concerned about housing costs. The architects have proposed a "Kiruna Portal" where materials from old houses can be recycled into new ones, but it's not clear if this will work.

Overall, Kiruna is facing an existential crisis due to the mine. The city has decided to move, and while this is an opportunity for reinvention, many residents are worried about their future.

Government surveillance programs collect a lot of personal information about people through their phone records. US researchers used this information to find out people's names, where they live, and even some private details.

Two scientists at Stanford University looked at "metadata" - information like who called whom, how long the call lasted, and when it happened. They matched this data with public information from services like Google, Yelp, and Facebook to learn more about people.

They found out things like one person owned a rifle, another had an irregular heartbeat, and someone was pregnant. They even discovered that someone with multiple sclerosis had made frequent calls to medical centers.

The researchers did this by collecting metadata from 823 volunteers who used an app on their phones. The app also got information from their Facebook accounts. This allowed the scientists to see how much private information they could find using just phone records and public data.

They showed that with a little bit of computer power, you can learn a lot about people's lives. They think this should make policymakers think twice before allowing mass surveillance programs.

The researchers also found out that if someone makes calls to certain places, like hospitals or pharmacies, you can infer what might be going on in their life. For example, they discovered that someone had made frequent calls to an abnormal heart-rate monitoring hotline.

The study's findings are important because they show how much private information is available through phone records and public data. They suggest that policymakers need to think about the balance between national security and people's civil liberties when it comes to surveillance programs.

As one expert said, "With the right analytics running over nation-scale communications data, you can infer huge amounts of sensitive information on everyone." The study provides numbers that discussions can now be based on.

Angela Erdmann never knew her grandfather, Richard Platz, because he died six years before she was born in 1946. But on April 8th, 2014, something amazing happened to her. She received a message from her grandfather that had been sent by him over 100 years ago.

The message was inside a brown beer bottle that was found floating in the Baltic Sea by a fisherman named Konrad Fischer. The bottle had been in the water for an incredible 101 years. A museum curator, Holger von Neuhoff, said this is likely the oldest message in a bottle ever found.

Richard Platz threw the bottle into the sea when he was just 20 years old on a hike with friends in 1913. He wrote a postcard that included his name and address in Berlin, and two stamps to cover the cost of sending it back to him. But what's amazing is that it took 101 years for someone to find it.

The postcard is mostly worn out, but Angela can still see her grandfather's handwriting. She was very moved by this discovery because she knew so little about her grandfather. He was a writer who believed in freedom and respect for others. He also loved culture and traveling, just like Angela.

Angela hopes that the bottle will stay at the museum after it goes on display until May 2014. Experts want to try and read more of the postcard's text. Angela wants to make pictures available so people can see what her grandfather looked like when he threw the bottle into the sea.

Every month, around 50,000 people in the UK go mystery shopping. They visit stores to check how well they are doing. This is because more and more people shop online, so stores want to make sure their physical shops offer a good experience.

Mystery shoppers can earn up to £155 per day. They usually spend eight hours visiting five to ten stores. Some even film their visits with hidden cameras in buttons or handbags. These video mystery shoppers can earn up to £300 per day.

Mystery shoppers are often reimbursed for money they spend in stores and may keep the products they buy. Laura, a 50-year-old mystery shopper from Devon, has visited over 7,000 shops since 2001. She earns around £30,000 to £40,000 per year, plus freebies.

Laura finds it satisfying to see improvements in stores she has visited before. However, competition for regular assignments is fierce. Many people are forced to work irregularly and earn lower pay. Some companies only offer a small fee or reimbursement for expenses.

A company called Marketforce relies on the promise of freebies to motivate its workers. They typically get £2-£5 per visit as a token gesture. A former mystery shopper, Val, says she gave up after three years because few assignments paid well enough to cover her bills.

However, some people are willing to work for minimal pay. Hannah, a City lawyer, has conducted nearly 500 visits without receiving payment or expenses. She is chosen by the Mystery Dining Company for exclusive assignments and enjoys fine dining experiences. But she must also spend two to four hours writing detailed reports after each visit, which can be challenging.

Over 1 million British workers might be employed under zero-hours contracts. This is more than previously thought. A recent survey by the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development found that many employers use these contracts.

Workers on zero-hours contracts often do not have a regular schedule, no holiday pay, or sick pay. They also need to ask permission before finding other work. However, some workers describe themselves as working full-time, even if they only work 30 hours or more per week.

The survey found that:

* One-third of organizations in the voluntary sector use zero-hours contracts.
* One-quarter of public sector organizations use them.
* Around 38% of people on these contracts say they are employed full-time.

The Office for National Statistics says around 250,000 workers in the UK have zero-hours contracts. However, this number might be too low.

Peter Cheese from the CIPD said we need to understand what zero-hours contracts mean and how they affect businesses and employees.

Some companies that use zero-hours contracts include:

* Sports Direct (20,000 staff)
* Cineworld (cinema chain)
* Buckingham Palace
* J D Wetherspoon (24,000 staff)

Unions and charities say employers are using these contracts to avoid paying benefits and treating workers unfairly. They say many workers have no choice but to accept them.

Workers on zero-hours contracts often don't know how much work they will get each week. They should be entitled to holiday pay, but not sick pay.

Some organizations, like the National Trust, use zero-hours contracts for seasonal workers because they need flexibility due to weather conditions.

Politician Chuka Umunna says these contracts should only be used in exceptional cases.

The CIPD research found that 16% of workers on zero-hours contracts often don't get enough hours each week. Industries like hotels and healthcare are more likely to use these contracts.

Vidhya Alakeson from the Resolution Foundation said we need a thorough review of zero-hours contracts by the government, taking into account their effects on workers' rights and well-being.

Tiger numbers have increased in Nepal. This is the highest number since the 1970s. A census showed that there are now 198 wild royal Bengal tigers in Nepal. This is a 63.6% increase in five years.

This news gives hope to conservationists who want to save the big cats. The number of tigers has been decreasing in south Asia for 100 years. Maheshwar Dhakal, an ecologist with Nepal's Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, said this is very encouraging.

The census used pictures from over 500 cameras placed in five protected areas and three wildlife corridors. More than 250 people worked on the survey, which cost about £250,000. A similar survey was conducted in India, but it will take a few more months to finalize the data.

Nepal has promised to double the number of tigers by 2022 from 121 in 2009. However, increasing prosperity in Asia has made tiger skins and body parts more valuable. This has led to many tigers being killed for their skin and bones, which are then sold in traditional Chinese medicine markets.

Conservation experts say that effective policing of national parks and stronger anti-poaching drives have helped increase the number of tigers. However, they also need to protect the habitat and animals that tigers prey on so they have enough space and food.

As tiger numbers have increased, there have been more conflicts between tigers and villagers. Seven people were killed by tigers in 2012 compared to four in 2011. Villagers are asking for better protection from tigers.

The government is making plans to protect tigers, but they also need to come up with plans to protect people who live near the national parks where tigers roam.

A tiger was captured in Chitwan after it killed two people, including a villager. There were once thousands of tigers in Bangladesh, India, and Nepal, but their numbers have dropped to about 3,000 over the past century.

Chitwan National Park has the highest number of adult tigers with 120, followed by Bardiya National Park with 50 and Shukla Phanta Wildlife Reserve with 17. Tiger skins are in demand in Tibet for festival costumes, while tiger bones are used in traditional Chinese medicine. The trade in tiger parts is very lucrative and fetches thousands of dollars on the black market.

Louise Haggerty, a 56-year-old hairdresser and waitress, went to a Sainsbury's supermarket in London on Black Friday at 1am with her friend. They wanted to buy a flat-screen TV for £149.99, but many people pushed to the front of the queue and they didn't get one.

Haggerty then bought a Dyson vacuum cleaner for £159.99, but she's not sure if she wants it. She said the store was very crowded and chaotic. "It was mental in there," she said. "People were behaving like animals."

Andy Blackett, 30, an estate agent, bought two TVs, two coffee makers, two tablets, and a stereo. He didn't know how much they cost, but he thought they were good deals.

However, his friend Henry Fischer, 19, wasn't as lucky. Someone took his TV from him because he was smaller than the other shoppers.

Police had to come to help at several stores, including Tesco's in London and Surrey Quays. At one store, customers tore down cardboard barriers and police delayed the sale of TVs until they could bring the situation under control.

One police officer said that the manager didn't have enough security and suggested suspending the sale. Two people were arrested at Black Friday sales events already that morning.

Some shoppers waited for hours in line to buy TVs, but not everyone was successful. Christine Ball, 62, had been waiting since 10:15pm and still hadn't got a TV. She wanted to buy one for her grandson for Christmas, but now she's not sure if it will happen.

Mel Mehmet, 23, has gone to Black Friday sales before, but this year the atmosphere at Tesco scared her. "It's crazy," she said. "Why do they have it at midnight? We're going to PC World in the morning instead."

Barack Obama wants young people to make changes in the world by working together despite their differences. He said this during his last visit to Britain as US president. 

Obama met with 500 young leaders in London and told them that they have the power to solve problems. “Our problems are made by humans, and we can fix them,” he said, quoting John F Kennedy. Obama encouraged the young people to use their skills to make a difference.

However, Obama also acknowledged that it's not easy being young today. He talked about big changes in the world, like terrorism and bad news on social media. But he said that this doesn't mean we should give up.

Obama wants young people to talk to people who have different opinions and beliefs. “Seek out people who don't agree with you,” he said. This will help them learn from each other and find solutions.

The president also talked about his time in office, including healthcare reforms and dealing with the 2008 financial crisis. He said that he's proud of what he achieved, but he knows there's still a lot to be done.

Obama met Jeremy Corbyn, the leader of the Labour party, before meeting David Cameron for golf. After his visit, Obama went to dinner with Cameron and the US ambassador.

Young people at the event were excited to hear from Obama. Some asked him questions about things like electoral rights and racial profiling at airports. Obama answered their questions and encouraged them to keep pushing for change.

Obama's message was clear: young people have the power to make a difference, but they need to work together and be patient. He quoted Dr Martin Luther King, saying that the path to justice is long but it will eventually bend towards fairness.

Millennials are very active on social media. In fact, 75% of them use some kind of social media platform. This is more than any other generation. However, not all millennials are the same. There are some who don't use social media at all.

Let's meet three millennials who have chosen to stay off social media:

Celan Beausoleil is a social worker from California. She used to be on Facebook but deleted her account in 2015 because she felt overwhelmed by all the information people shared online. "It was too heavy for me," she said. But she likes how social media connects people around the world.

Mathias, who works for the Baltimore City government, deleted his Facebook and Twitter accounts in 2012. He realized he spent too much time scrolling through newsfeeds and not enough time reading books or talking to friends. Now, he enjoys the free time and spends it on more meaningful activities.

Lauren Raskauskas, a 22-year-old from Florida, is also private about her online presence. She deleted her Twitter account and deactivated her Facebook account because she didn't want people to know what she was doing all the time. "I'm more concerned about my privacy," she said. However, she understands the benefits of social media and how it can help connect people.

Rajagopalan is a student at Boston College who has never been on social media before college. He joined Facebook just to contact his roommate but hasn't used it since. "I don't really need one to read tweets," he said, referring to Twitter. He prefers to stay off social media and focus on real-life relationships.

These millennials show that there's no one-size-fits-all approach when it comes to social media use. Some people enjoy the benefits of being online, while others prefer to stay private and offline.

Large carnivores like brown bears, wolves, and lynx are thriving in Europe despite being feared to be on the brink of extinction due to human population growth and overconsumption. A new study published in Science has found that these predators' populations are stable or increasing across the continent.

Brown bears, wolves, Eurasian lynx, and wolverines can be found in almost one-third of mainland Europe, living outside nature reserves. There are around 17,000 brown bears, 12,000 wolves, 9,000 Eurasian lynx, and 1,250 wolverines in Europe.

The study's lead author, Guillaume Chapron from Sweden's University of Agricultural Sciences, found that wolves can live in areas with up to 3,050 people per square kilometre. This shows that even densely populated regions like the UK could support big predators.

Chapron believes that a "land-sharing" model of conservation is key to their success. This means allowing humans and wildlife to coexist rather than keeping them apart by fencing off wilderness areas. The researchers think this approach could be applied elsewhere in the world.

The EU Habitats Directive, which protects rare species, has played a crucial role in Europe's large carnivore revival. Author George Monbiot welcomes the trend but notes that Britain is an exception due to its history of persecution and lack of conservation efforts.

Monbiot thinks there's no reason why the UK can't see a similar return of wildlife, citing examples like bears and wolves living near Rome. A campaign is underway to reintroduce lynx into Scotland's Cairngorms region, which could be a step towards restoring Britain's natural balance.

Doñana National Park in southern Spain is an important site for birdlife in western Europe. The park is home to many migratory birds from Africa and Britain, as well as some of Europe's rarest birds like the Spanish imperial eagle. However, it also has a highly endangered mammal, the Iberian lynx.

In 1998, a disaster happened when contaminated water poured into the park from a nearby mine. This caused a big problem for the environment and killed many birds and fish. The clean-up cost €90m, but Spain decided to spend even more money (€360m) to restore the landscape.

The park used to be drained in some places to create rice and cotton fields, but now it is being returned to its original wetland state. This has been a costly process, but it's been successful so far.

However, there are still many threats to Doñana National Park. There are plans to build an oil pipeline through the park, which could harm the environment. Additionally, developers want to expand tourist resorts in the area, which would require more water and potentially damage the local ecosystem.

A recent decision by the Andalucían government has caused concern among conservationists. They have decided to reopen a mine that almost destroyed Doñana National Park in 1998. This is worrying because it could lead to another environmental disaster.

The government says they will use modern mining techniques, which are safer for the environment. However, some people are still opposed to reopening the mine. They think it's not worth the risk of harming the park and its inhabitants.

One expert from the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) said: "Doñana already faces many threats, but now they want to bring back the cause of its near-undoing 16 years ago. It is extremely worrying."

Another expert, Carlos Dávila, works for the Spanish Ornithological Society in Doñana. He said: "This is a very bad idea indeed. They say the new mine will be safe, but they said it was safe in 1998 and look what happened."

The reopening of the mine has also caused concern among local people who support eco-tourism in the area. Many visitors come to see the park's amazing birdlife, which is a big source of income for the local community.

One local resident said: "This is Europe's most precious bird sanctuary. We can't afford to risk losing it again."

**Tipping in the UK**

The government is looking at changing rules about tipping in restaurants. Currently, there's no law that says tips must go to workers. A review found that some waiters are charged 15% for using credit or debit cards to receive tips. Some employers make workers pay back these fees if they don't get enough tips.

**What Waiters Think**

We talked to four waiters about tipping in the UK:

1. **Rodri (37, London)**: Rodri says around half of a waiter's income comes from tips. He thinks restaurants should clearly show their tip policy so customers know what they're getting into.
2. **Elle (22, Edinburgh)**: Elle works three jobs and gets different amounts of tips each job. She says it's hard to know if she's getting her fair share because she doesn't see how much is being tipped through card payments. Elle thinks the tipping system in France is better.
3. **Ashley (22, London)**: Ashley says that sometimes their tips go towards customer breakages, which isn't fair. She wants managers to find another way to pay for broken things without taking money from workers' tips.
4. **Tom (Manchester)**: Tom used to work in a restaurant where floor staff kept 80% of cash tips and 40% of card tips. He thinks the tipping system is better in Italy, where people often round up their bill to show appreciation.

**What's Being Proposed**

The government is considering proposals that would:

* Stop employers from charging workers an administration fee for receiving tips
* Make restaurants clearly display their tip policy
* Ensure customers know that tips are voluntary

**What Waiters Want**

Waiters want a more transparent tipping system, where they can see how much money they're getting and how it's being used. Some think restaurants should pay a good basic wage so workers don't have to rely on tips to make ends meet.

**Examples from Around the World**

* In the US, waiters often get a fair share of tips
* In France, waiting tables is seen as a proper job with decent income and job security
* In Italy, people round up their bill to show appreciation for good service
* In Australia, workers are paid a good basic wage so they don't have to rely on tips

**Changes in British Eating Habits Over 40 Years**

A recent survey by the UK government looked at how people's eating habits have changed over time. The study involved 150,000 households from 1974 to 2014.

**Less Tea and More Coffee**

In the past, tea was a big part of British culture, with people drinking an average of 68g per person per week in the 1970s. Now, this has dropped to just 25g per person per week, which means people drink about eight cups of tea a week on average.

**More Healthy Food Choices**

While some unhealthy foods like chips and pizza have become more popular, there are also signs that people are making healthier choices. For example, consumption of fresh fruit has increased by 50% since the 1970s.

**Changes in Bread Consumption**

The way people eat bread has also changed over time. While white bread was once a staple, now brown and wholemeal bread is more popular. People are eating fewer slices of bread per week than they used to, from an average of 25 slices to just 15.

**More Takeaway Food**

Takeaway food has become much more popular in the UK over the past 40 years, with consumption almost doubling since the 1970s. Most takeaway food is either chips or meat-based meals.

**Fruit and Veg Consumption**

While some unhealthy foods have increased in popularity, fruit and vegetable consumption has also risen significantly. People are eating an average of 157g of fruit per day, which is close to the recommended five-a-day amount.

**Other Changes**

Some other changes that emerged from the survey include:

* Less people keep chickens for eggs
* More people buy food online
* People spend a smaller proportion of their income on food (11% compared to 24% in the 1970s)

**What It Means**

The UK Environment Secretary, Elizabeth Truss, said: "Food is at the heart of our society and this data shows how we've changed over time. We're more interested in where our food comes from and what's in it."

She hopes that by making this data available, people can learn more about their eating habits and make better choices for themselves and their families.

**Key Statistics:**

* Tea consumption has dropped from 68g to 25g per person per week
* Fresh fruit consumption has increased by 50% since the 1970s
* Takeaway food consumption has almost doubled since the 1970s
* People eat an average of 157g of fruit per day
* Bread consumption has decreased, with fewer slices eaten per week
* People spend a smaller proportion of their income on food (11% compared to 24% in the 1970s)

Agios Efstratios is a small island in Greece that is very far away from the mainland. There are no mobile phone networks or ATMs on the island, so people have to rely on cash. Before Greece had financial problems, residents of Agios Efstratios did their banking at the post office and tourism was strong.

But now, with banks closed, it's hard for residents to get money. They have to travel nine hours to another island just to withdraw cash. This is making it difficult for tourists to visit, as numbers are down 80% this year. Even people who were born on the island but live in Athens aren't coming because of the difficulties.

The mayor of Agios Efstratios, Maria Kakali, is trying to get an ATM installed, but she's worried that it might be too late for this season. Tourism is the main source of income on the island, and without it, people will struggle.

There are also bigger problems ahead because the government plans to end a tax break that has been in place for decades. This tax break was created to help small islands survive by reducing sales taxes. If it's removed, prices on the island could rise even more than they already have, making it harder for residents and tourists alike.

The situation is also affecting people under 40 who are trying to make a living on the island. Many of them work multiple jobs just to get by, but still can't afford families or save money. They're worried that if taxes go up, even more young people will leave the island in search of better opportunities.

Mayor Kakali is fighting against the tax rise and hopes that it might be delayed until 2017 when Agios Efstratios is exempt from the increase. If not, she plans to take a group of children from her school to the parliament building in Athens to remind the government about the impact the tax rise will have on their island community.

Some of the key statistics mentioned include:

* 80% decrease in tourist numbers this year
* Residents have to make nine-hour round trips to withdraw cash
* Agios Efstratios has around 200 residents and is one of the smallest islands in Greece
* The tax break will increase prices by up to 23%
* The island's economy is fragile, with only three shops, two restaurants, and no official hotels.

Scientists have made a major breakthrough by connecting the brains of two animals, allowing them to share information with each other. This is an important step towards creating what they call an "organic computer".

The team from the US used special devices called brain-to-brain interfaces to connect two rats. The rats were trained to work together on simple tasks, such as pressing a lever when a light went on above it. When they succeeded, they received a drink of water.

In one experiment, the scientists connected two rats separated by thousands of miles, with one in North Carolina and the other in Brazil. They used the internet to link their brains together.

The researchers showed that the rats can share and act on each other's sensory information. For example, if one rat saw a light, it could send a signal to the other rat's brain, which would then press the lever.

Interestingly, the communication between the rats was two-way. If one rat failed at the task, the other rat would adjust its behaviour to make it easier for its partner.

The team is now working on linking several animals' brains together to solve more complex tasks. They believe that a combination of brains could provide solutions that individual brains cannot achieve alone.

Anders Sandberg, an expert in neurotechnologies, said that this research is important because it helps us understand how brains encode information. He also believes that the technology has broader implications for communication and coordination.

However, he added that there's no risk of supersmart rats or a "rat multiborg" invasion. The technology is still in its early stages, and much more research needs to be done before it can be used in people.

Very little is known about how thoughts are encoded and transmitted into another person's brain, so this is not a realistic prospect for now. Sandberg also pointed out that most of our thoughts are just "drafts" or ideas that we haven't acted on yet, and it would be confusing to have access to those thoughts.

This breakthrough has the potential to change how we understand communication and coordination in animals, including humans.

Thousands of people protested on Australia's beaches against killing sharks off the coast of Western Australia. They want the government to stop this plan, called a cull. The prime minister and famous people like Richard Branson are also against it.

Some people were killed by sharks in Western Australia two years ago. But the country has only had an average of one shark-related death per year for the last 50 years. A group called Sea Shepherd says that killing more sharks will not make beaches safer.

People from all over Australia protested on beaches, including in Perth, Sydney, Adelaide, and other cities. They say Australians love sharks and want to protect them. Some people who surf said that killing sharks won't stop attacks because there are already too many people in the water.

The government says they will not say how many sharks they have killed, but some people think they might be releasing smaller sharks back into the ocean. Experts say there is no proof that killing more sharks will make beaches safer. In fact, it could bring more predators to the area.

In 2012, worldwide there were only 80 shark attacks, and seven of them were fatal. But every year, humans kill nearly 100 million sharks. RSPCA Australia says they think the cull is a bad idea because it won't work.

Richard Branson said that killing sharks will actually harm tourism in Western Australia. He thinks people don't want to visit beaches where sharks are being killed.

**The Last Male Northern White Rhino**

There is only one male northern white rhino left in the world, named Sudan. He lives at Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Kenya with two female northern white rhinos. If Sudan doesn't mate with one of these females soon, there will be no more northern white rhinos born.

Sudan is 42 years old and has not been able to breed successfully so far. There are only three other northern white rhinos in the world: two females in zoos and a female at Ol Pejeta Conservancy with Sudan.

**Protecting Sudan**

Armed guards watch over Sudan day and night to protect him from poachers who want to kill him for his horn. They believe that the horn has medicinal properties, although this is not true. Sudan's horn was even cut off to try to stop the poachers, but they are still a threat.

**A Vulnerable Species**

Sudan looks like a strong and powerful animal, but he is actually very vulnerable. His home is in danger, and there are many people who want to hurt him. This is not just about Sudan - it's also about other northern white rhinos that have been killed or captured by poachers.

**The History of Rhino Hunting**

Humans have been killing rhinos for thousands of years. In the past, they hunted them for their meat and hides, but now they are mostly killed for their horns. The demand for rhino horn is very high in some countries, which means that more and more rhinos are being killed.

**The Current Situation**

There are only a few hundred northern white rhinos left in the world, and many other types of African rhinos are also under threat. Poachers are killing them at an alarming rate, and it's not clear if anything can be done to stop them.

**A Lesson from the Past**

Humans have been killing the things we love for a long time. We have learned that this is not sustainable and that we must protect our planet and its creatures. But despite this knowledge, we are still hurting many animals, including rhinos.

An agreement to improve safety in Bangladesh's factories is facing problems. Factory owners want compensation for closing their factories temporarily to fix problems. They say it costs too much to pay staff while they're closed, and that some repairs will take months.

This issue started after the Rana Plaza building collapsed in 2013, killing 1,138 people. Now, hundreds of factories are inspected each month to make sure they meet safety standards. The Accord on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh is a group of international brands, trade unions, and Bangladeshi factory owners working together.

One factory owner, from Softex Cotton, has threatened to take legal action against the Accord because his factory was closed due to structural problems. He wants $100 million in compensation.

Some factory owners say that if a factory closes temporarily, it will lose orders and eventually close permanently. They think the Accord agreement didn't clearly explain who would pay for closures.

Jenny Holdcroft, from IndustriALL, said the Accord ensures that factories won't lose orders during closure because brands have promised to keep ordering from them for two years. She also said that many factories only need partial closure to fix problems and that workers will be paid during factory closures.

However, some people think the Accord should contribute more money to help pay displaced workers. A rival group called the Alliance has set aside $5 million to help pay workers for up to two months while repairs are done. This has caused confusion among factory owners, who want the Accord to also contribute.

Shaidullah Azim, a director of the Bangladeshi Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, said that the Alliance is helping workers by sharing their salaries with entrepreneurs. He wants the Accord to do the same so they can help their workers too.

The world's richest people are making too much money and this is causing big problems. The charity Oxfam says that the huge amounts of money made by the 100 wealthiest billionaires are increasing inequality and stopping us from fighting poverty. 

Oxfam says that if these billionaires gave away all the money they earned in 2012, it would be enough to help millions of people out of poverty four times over. The charity also argues that the huge income gap between the rich and poor is holding back growth and hurting the environment.

In a report called "The Cost of Inequality", Oxfam says that the richest 1% of people have increased their incomes by 60% in the past 20 years, which is faster than before. This has led to problems like low investment, slow growth, and high levels of pollution.

Oxfam's Chief Executive, Barbara Stocking, says that extreme wealth can be bad for everyone because it leads to social divisions, economic inefficiencies, and environmental damage. She believes that countries need to work together to reduce inequality and make sure the benefits of wealth are shared more equally.

The report shows that inequality is a problem all around the world. In the UK, poverty levels are increasing again, just like in the time of Charles Dickens. In China, the top 10% of people now earn nearly 60% of the income, which is similar to South Africa, one of the most unequal countries on earth.

In the US, the top 1% of earners get twice as much money as they did in 1980, and for the richest 0.01%, it's even worse than during the 1920s. The World Bank and International Monetary Fund agree that extreme income inequality is bad for growth and have tried to limit it.

Oxfam says that world leaders should learn from countries like Brazil, which has grown rapidly while reducing inequality. They also suggest closing tax havens, which hold as much as $31 trillion of money, could bring in an extra $189 billion in taxes.

Important:

* The richest 100 billionaires made $240 billion in 2012.
* If they gave away this money, it would be enough to help millions of people out of poverty four times over.
* The richest 1% have increased their incomes by 60% in the past 20 years.
* Inequality is a problem all around the world, including in the UK, China, and the US.
* Extreme income inequality can lead to social divisions, economic inefficiencies, and environmental damage.

UK Prime Minister David Cameron says Scotland has voted to stay part of the United Kingdom. The vote showed that 55.3% of people wanted Scotland to remain part of the UK, while 44.7% wanted it to be independent. This means that Scotland will not become an independent country.

Cameron promised to make changes in how England is governed, including giving more power to English members of parliament at Westminster. He said this would happen after the next general election. The Scottish government had asked for more control over issues like taxes and welfare, but Cameron didn't say exactly when these changes would come.

The Labour leader, Ed Miliband, said that Scotland's vote was a call for change in how the UK is governed. He promised to give Scotland more power and also make changes across England, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

The deputy prime minister, Nick Clegg, said that the referendum marked a new chapter for Scotland within the UK and wider constitutional reform across the union. However, this decision may not be the end of debates about Scottish independence.

Some Conservative MPs are unhappy with Cameron's promise to increase Scotland's powers, while the leader of the UK Independence Party, Nigel Farage, thinks that England needs more power and protection from decisions made by Scottish MPs.

Cameron and the Queen will make statements to calm tensions. The prime minister wants to show that the three main party leaders will keep their promises made during the referendum campaign.

Brazil's famous singer Anitta has many fans worldwide. She makes music called funk that originated in the favelas (poor neighborhoods) of Brazil. However, some people say she has changed her appearance to fit into the richer and whiter part of Brazilian society.

Anitta was compared before and after she signed a big contract with a music company. Her skin looked darker when she was unknown, but now it looks paler. Some think this is because of makeup or plastic surgery, while others believe it's just Photoshopping on her pictures.

Anti-discrimination campaigners say Anitta had to change her appearance to fit into the mainly white middle-class market. They claim that in Brazil, being white means you are richer and more successful, while being black is associated with poverty and failure.

Anitta was born Larissa de Macedo Machado and started singing in church choirs as a child. She became famous for her hit single "Show das Poderosas" which got 52 million views on YouTube.

Some people think Anitta has toned down the provocative dancing and lyrics of funk music to appeal to a wider audience. However, others believe she has gone too far by changing her image to fit into the richer and whiter part of society.

This is a sensitive topic in Brazil because many Brazilians are mixed-race and there's a link between skin tone and inequality. White people earn twice as much as black or mixed-race people, and most business executives are white while most menial jobs are done by black or mixed-race workers.

A psychology student named Jarid Arraes wrote that Anitta's image change shows how Brazil is still a discriminatory society that doesn't support diversity. A lecturer at the Federal University of Pernambuco said Anitta has won over the middle class by taking a rebellious sound and making it more palatable to everyone.

Others disagree, saying the issue of color is overblown and that Anitta's image change is just about her personal style and preferences. An activist from Salvador said the prejudice lies with music producers and media executives, not with society as a whole.

Anitta has described the need for identity to be self-defined, saying that she tries to show people that they can be who they want to be without needing to fit into certain stereotypes.

Pope Benedict XVI resigned as the head of the Catholic Church on a cold Monday in February 2013. He did this in a quiet and simple way, like an old man who can no longer work because of his back pain. Before he left, he told a group of cardinals that they would have to choose a new Pope.

The Mexican Monsignor Oscar Sanchéz Barba was present at the meeting. He had come to Rome for another important event and heard the Pope's announcement. "We were all surprised," said Monsignor Sanchéz Barba. The cardinals looked at each other in shock, not believing what they had just heard.

The Dean of the College of Cardinals, Angelo Sodano, gave a short speech to assure the Pope that they would support him and respect his decision. Then the Pope blessed everyone and left.

John Thavis, a journalist who has written about the Vatican for 30 years, had predicted that the Pope might resign. He thought it was likely to happen on February 22, but it actually happened two days later.

People are saying that the Pope's decision is brave because he is willing to face reality and admit that he is no longer able to do his job. The Vatican says that contemporary medicine can keep people alive for a long time, but the Pope wants to be honest about his age and abilities.

However, some people are speculating that there might be another reason why the Pope resigned. They wonder if something was going to come out about his past. The Vatican denies this, but it's understandable that people would think this way.

A woman named Julia Rochester, who is a lapsed Catholic, was thinking about what the Pope's resignation means. She asked herself, "If you're God's chosen one, how do you choose not be chosen?" Many Catholics will be asking themselves this question in the weeks ahead.

The Chemin des Dunes school is located in a refugee camp outside Calais, France. Despite its simple conditions - a plastic roof held up by a tree trunk and some desks made from old chairs - the students study very hard. They hope to learn French well enough to start a new life in France.

Kamal, a 29-year-old electrical engineer from Sudan's Darfur region, is one of the students. He says, "The French language is difficult, but we try our best. If we come every day, maybe we can achieve our dreams." Kamal comes to class for three or four hours each day.

There are many refugees in the camp who want to stay in France, not go to the UK. However, media coverage only focuses on those trying to cross the Channel. In fact, France has taken in over 250,000 refugees, which is more than twice as many as the UK.

The school was started by Zimarco Jones, a Nigerian man who arrived in Calais in 2013 and is still waiting for his asylum claim to be processed. The school offers free classes in French, English, art, and t'ai chi. There are also volunteers from Calais and beyond who help teach the students.

One student, George, says he wanted to go to the UK because he speaks fluent English. However, after taking language classes, he is happy to stay in France. He says, "Anywhere there is peace, I can stay."

Many of the teachers are local volunteers who give up their summer holidays to help the refugees. One teacher, Jenny Flahaut, says she wants to show people that migrants are not like they are portrayed in the media.

The school has big plans for the future. Zimarco wants to set up a separate classroom for women and children, as well as a football team for migrants. He also dreams of changing the name of the camp from "the jungle" to something more positive.

In Canada's Arctic region, where the sun shines brightly for over 20 hours a day in summer, Muslims face a unique challenge during Ramadan. They must fast from dawn to sunset, but since it gets light so late and stays light so long, this can be difficult.

Abdul Karim, a Muslim living in Iqaluit, Nunavut, has found a way to adapt to the long days of summer. He eats before sunrise at 1:30 am and breaks his fast after sunset at 11 pm. "I haven't fainted yet," he jokes, showing that he is careful about his health.

Most Muslims in Iqaluit follow the same schedule as those in Ottawa, which is 1,300 miles south. This means fasting for around 18 hours a day. Some people break their fast together with friends and family at the new mosque in Iqaluit.

In Yellowknife, another Arctic city, the Muslim community has different options for fasting during Ramadan. They can follow the schedule of nearby cities or the timings of Mecca and Medina. Some people opt to follow the schedule of Edmonton, which is about 15 hours shorter than Ottawa's.

In Inuvik, a small town north of the Arctic Circle, there is constant sunlight throughout the year. The Muslim community follows the schedule of Edmonton, as it would be impossible to fast according to the local sun. They try to strike a balance between Ramadan and their local culture by including traditional foods in their iftar meal.

For Muslims living in the Arctic, Ramadan can be challenging due to the long days. However, they are determined to follow the holy month's traditions despite the difficulties. One Muslim, Abdul Karim, is looking forward to future years when Ramadan will fall during the winter months and the sun rises and sets within a few hours each day.

Important dates and times:

* Abdul Karim eats before sunrise at 1:30 am
* He breaks his fast after sunset at 11 pm
* The Muslim community in Iqaluit follows the schedule of Ottawa, fasting for around 18 hours a day
* Some people in Yellowknife follow the schedule of Edmonton, which is about 15 hours shorter than Ottawa's

The Senate Intelligence Committee has approved a new law that will allow the National Security Agency (NSA) to continue collecting phone records from millions of Americans. However, this collection will now be subject to more transparency and oversight. 

The bill was sponsored by Chairwoman Dianne Feinstein and allows the NSA to keep phone metadata for 90 days at a time. This data can then be searched if there is a "reasonable suspicion" that someone is connected to international terrorism.

Some lawmakers are concerned about this new law, saying it does not go far enough in limiting the NSA's power. Senator Mark Udall said, "The NSA's surveillance of Americans' private information does not respect our constitutional values and needs fundamental reform."

However, Feinstein believes that the NSA bulk collection program is necessary for national security. She said, "The NSA call-records program is legal and subject to congressional oversight, but more can be done to increase transparency and build public trust."

The bill also makes some improvements to transparency and oversight, such as requiring an annual report on the number of times the program leads to investigations or probable cause orders.

Despite this approval, there are still concerns about the NSA's actions. Senator Ron Wyden said, "This bill maintains business as usual and remains far from meaningful reform." He also expressed concern about recent reports that the NSA has been intercepting data between Google and Yahoo servers.

Feinstein surprised many by saying she is "totally opposed" to the NSA's surveillance of foreign leaders, including German Chancellor Angela Merkel. She had previously supported this practice.

The stage is now set for a showdown with another bill, introduced by Senator Patrick Leahy, which would prohibit bulk collection of Americans' phone records.

Noise from ships can hurt animals like killer whales and dolphins more than we thought. New research shows that this noise can stop them from communicating with each other and finding food. The noise is not just loud, it's also at the right frequency for these animals to hear. 

The researchers studied 1,600 ships passing through a strait in Washington State using underwater microphones. They found that the average noise level was as loud as a rock concert. But when whales are far away from the ships, they would still hear about the same amount of noise as a lawnmower or vacuum cleaner.

This is a problem because whales and dolphins need to be able to communicate with each other to find food. If they can't do this, they will have to use up their extra fat reserves, which contain pollutants that are bad for them. 

The researchers say that we should try to make ships quieter. Military ships are already quieter than commercial ones, so there must be ways to transfer the technology to make commercial ships quieter too. We could also slow down the ships to reduce the noise.

A lot of whales are in danger due to various reasons. The US government has protected a big area in the Atlantic Ocean to save the North Atlantic right whale, which is critically endangered. In Europe, killer whales have high levels of pollutants in their bodies. Scientists are trying to figure out if these pollutants caused the deaths of five sperm whales that got stuck on the coast of Britain last year.

Around Australia, whales face threats from ship strikes and oil and gas drilling. Japan has also said it will start whaling again in Antarctic waters.

Important note: There are only 84 killer whales foraging up the US west coast and into Puget Sound, making them a vulnerable population.

Scientists have studied DNA from a 7,000-year-old European hunter-gatherer's wisdom tooth. This has given them a unique look at what modern humans were like before farming started.

The man likely had dark skin, black or brown hair, and blue eyes. He probably couldn't digest lactose and starchy foods well. In contrast, people who began farming around that time were able to eat more types of food.

When farming started, humans and animals came into closer contact, which led to more infections. However, the hunter-gatherer's DNA showed that he already had genetic mutations that helped fight off diseases. Some of these mutations still exist in modern Europeans today.

A team of scientists from Spain discovered the man's DNA after finding two skeletons in a cave in 2006. The men were around 30 years old and lived before farming arrived in Europe.

The scientists focused on one skeleton and managed to reconstruct his entire genome from DNA found in his wisdom tooth. This is the first time they have done this for someone who lived before the Neolithic revolution.

The study's leader, Carles Lalueza-Fox, was surprised by what he found. The man had gene variants that would have produced darker skin than any modern European. He also had blue eyes, which was unexpected because this trait is thought to have developed later than lighter skin colour.

This research suggests that the evolution of humans and their immune systems is more complex than previously thought. It may not be entirely true that farming made people sicker.

The study also found that the hunter-gatherer's DNA matched closely with modern Europeans from northern Europe, such as Sweden and Finland.

Martin Jones, a professor at Cambridge University, said that the most interesting part of the study is the discovery of genetic mutations that helped fight off diseases. This challenges the idea that farming was bad for human health.

This research could change how artists draw people who lived during this time period. Instead of depicting them as having light skin and blue eyes, they may be more accurate to show darker skin and blue eyes.

The study also raises questions about what kinds of diseases these ancient people might have had.
