Chemists have been waiting a long time for new elements to be discovered. And finally, four new elements were found in Japan, Russia, and the US. These elements, numbers 113, 115, 117, and 118, complete the periodic table's seventh row.

The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) verified these new elements on December 30, 2015. They came from studies done between 2004 and 2015. The scientists who found them need to give their names a formal title. Currently, they are called ununtrium, ununpentium, ununseptium, and ununoctium.

The IUPAC said that the Russian-American team at Joint Institute for Nuclear Research in Dubna and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California discovered elements 115, 117, and 118. They also gave credit to a Japanese team from RIKEN Institute for discovering element 113.

According to IUPAC rules, new elements can be named after mythological concepts, minerals, places, countries, or scientists. For example, elements 114 and 116 were named flerovium and livermorium in 2012.

The Japanese team is considering three names for ununtrium: japonium, rikenium, and nishinarium. They will choose one name after a review by IUPAC.

Scientists must also propose two-letter symbols for the elements. When they do this, the proposals will be put up for public review for five months. This way, scientists and others can raise any objections.

To discover these new elements, researchers at three labs slammed lighter nuclei into each other and looked for signature radioactive decays that come from the new elements. It's hard to know what kind of element they are because very few atoms have been made.

The verification process means that scientists will now be able to study these elements more closely. This can help them understand how they work and even lead to technological advances in making observations. But it may take a long time for practical applications of the new elements to appear.

Prince Harry has left Afghanistan after spending four months there. During this time, he was in charge of an Apache helicopter and helped protect ground troops from the Taliban. He also admitted to shooting at insurgents while on his missions.

In interviews with the media, Prince Harry spoke about how difficult it is for him to balance being a member of the royal family with being a soldier. He explained that he has three different roles: one as a soldier, one in his private life, and one as a member of the royal family.

Prince Harry also criticized some parts of the media, including The Sun, Daily Mail, and Daily Telegraph, for how they report on him and his family. He said that these papers often write negative things about him and that it can be upsetting.

The prince has been in Afghanistan before, four years ago, but this time he was able to keep a lower profile thanks to an agreement with the Ministry of Defence. Only a few media outlets were allowed to report on his deployment, and they had to agree not to follow him around all the time.

Prince Harry said that he prefers being referred to as Captain Wales rather than Prince Harry because it makes him feel more like one of the soldiers he is working with. He also talked about how his father, Prince Charles, often reminds him to behave in a way that is fitting for a member of the royal family.

Before going to Afghanistan, Prince Harry was involved in another media controversy when pictures emerged of him playing naked in Las Vegas during a private party. He said that he had let himself down and others by not being more careful about his actions.

A new scientific study says that if we do not stop releasing greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, the Earth's temperature will rise by at least 4 degrees Celsius by 2100. This is twice as much as what the world's governments consider safe.

The researcher leading this study, Professor Steven Sherwood from Australia, says that fewer clouds are forming in a warmer world. This means less sunlight is being reflected back into space, and temperatures will continue to rise even more.

Clouds play a big role in how much the Earth warms up, but scientists have not fully understood their effects until now. The new study shows that clouds can make global warming worse than expected.

A 4-degree temperature increase would be very bad for many parts of the world, especially the tropics. It could also cause the polar ice caps to melt, leading to a big rise in sea levels.

Scientists are encouraged by this study because it helps us understand how much greenhouse gases affect the Earth's climate. However, they still need more research to make accurate predictions about future temperatures.

The study found that the main reason for uncertainty in temperature predictions is clouds. To fix this, researchers used computer models that take into account how clouds really work in the real world.

These models show that if we do not stop releasing greenhouse gases, the Earth's average air temperature will rise by between 3 and 5 degrees Celsius by 2100. This is a more accurate prediction than previous estimates.

Some people have criticized climate change models for being wrong, but this study shows that they are actually too conservative. The researchers say that we should take action to reduce our greenhouse gas emissions urgently because the consequences of inaction will be severe.

Making Cities More Livable: 10 Creative Solutions

Cities can be challenging places to live, with pollution, traffic, and lack of green spaces. But some people are coming up with innovative ideas to make our cities more livable.

1. Pop-up Parks
Imagine turning an empty car park into a mini park! This idea started in San Francisco as an arts project and has spread worldwide. People can create their own parks using pots, plants, and a little creativity.

2. Underground Bike Sheds
Not everyone loves cars. In Tokyo, a company called Giken invented an underground bike shed that stores up to 204 bikes safely and securely. Owners can retrieve their bikes with just one touch of a button.

3. Glow-in-the-Dark Trees
Daan Roosegaarde, a Dutch designer, created a tree that glows in the dark using special DNA from marine bacteria. He hopes this technology will one day replace streetlights.

4. Footfall Harvesting
In London's West Ham area, people walk on special tiles that capture energy from their footsteps and power the streetlights above. This system is also used at airports like Heathrow.

5. Supertrees
These tall, steel-framed trees in Singapore can grow flowers, ferns, and even solar panels! They absorb heat and provide air ventilation for nearby buildings.

6. Water-Producing Billboard
A team of researchers created a billboard that traps humidity from the air to produce up to 96 liters of drinking water per day. People can help themselves to it for free!

7. Living Walls
Gardens are no longer just on front lawns; now they're on walls! Companies like Biotecture create "living walls" using hydroponics, which reduce air pollution and improve air quality.

8. Algae-Powered Building
In Hamburg, a building uses algae to produce electricity. The algae photosynthesize on the building's facades and are harvested to power homes.

9. Smart Rubbish Bins
Cities are switching from traditional trash cans to solar-powered "trash compactors" that notify collectors when they're full. These bins can store up to 150 gallons of rubbish!

10. Green Spray for Grass
In some Chinese cities, authorities are using a non-toxic green spray to brighten up yellowing grass. This might not be the most conventional solution, but it's working!

The future of transportation is changing quickly. Experts say that economic, demographic, and technological changes are making it necessary for cities to rethink how people move around.

As people commute longer distances and city infrastructure gets older, cities like Los Angeles, Seattle, and Chicago are trying new ways to make travel easier and more sustainable. They're adding more bus lanes, improving pedestrian walkways, and developing self-driving cars that can communicate with each other and their surroundings.

This "intelligent" transportation system is expected to become a key part of city planning. Experts like Robert Puentes say that cities need robust transportation networks to be competitive globally.

Here are three trends that will shape the future of transportation:

1. Ride-sharing services like Uber and Lyft, and apps like Waze, which helps drivers find the fastest routes.
2. Vehicle-to-vehicle data communication, which allows cars to talk to each other and traffic control systems.
3. Self-driving cars, which could reduce accidents and emissions.

According to a study, younger people are driving less than previous generations. Those born in the 1990s make 4% fewer car trips and travel 18% fewer miles per year than their parents did at the same age.

The rise of ride-sharing services has also led to more traffic in residential neighborhoods, which is a problem for residents who value peace and quiet.

Experts are working on technology that will allow vehicles to communicate with each other and infrastructure, like traffic lights. This could lead to smoother traffic flow and reduced congestion.

Driverless cars have been tested since 2012, but they won't become common anytime soon. However, partial automation of cars is already happening, starting with automated buses and trucks in specific areas.

Automated transportation has the potential to improve safety, reduce emissions, and increase access to cars for more people. But it will take time to implement given that many cars on the road are old.

As countries work to meet ambitious climate goals, policies could promote zero-emission vehicles, walking, biking, and carpooling. Sharon Feigon envisions a future where people can use one transit pass to access multiple modes of transportation.

It's also important to consider why people travel: for work, social reasons, or shopping. Technologies that reduce the need for trips, like virtual meetings, could have a big impact on transportation.

The future of transportation is exciting and full of possibilities. It's an opportunity to create more sustainable, efficient, and connected cities that meet the needs of their residents.

Every morning, before it gets too hot in Delhi, some friends get together on the grass near India Gate. They stretch, breathe deeply, and meditate. Arvind Singh, a 42-year-old salesman, thinks this is the best way to start the day. "It's much better than eating an egg or a sandwich," he said.

Many people in India are doing yoga like this every morning. The Indian government is encouraging it too. On June 21st, the new International Day of Yoga, thousands of people will gather at India Gate for a big yoga session. Even the prime minister, Narendra Modi, will join in.

Modi wants to make yoga popular all over the world. He has asked schools to teach yoga to their students and has also suggested that police officers should do yoga regularly. Some airlines are even offering free yoga lessons to their staff.

Yoga is an ancient Indian practice that helps people connect with their bodies and minds. It's not just about exercise, but also about finding peace and balance in life. The Indian government thinks that if more people practice yoga, it can help reduce violence and pollution in the country.

Some critics say that Modi is promoting a particular view of India that doesn't include other cultures. They think that yoga has become too commercialized. However, others point out that a US court recently ruled that yoga classes don't have to be linked to any particular faith.

Author Amish Tripathi thinks that yoga is something that everyone can enjoy, regardless of their religion or culture. "It's a gift from ancient India," he said. Another expert, Suneel Singh, agrees. "Yoga is not just for Hindus or Indians; it's for everyone who wants to stay healthy and happy."

Harvey Goldsmith, a famous music promoter, thinks that the UK's biggest summer music festivals are nearing their end. He believes that there aren't enough new popular bands to replace the old ones.

Goldsmith has worked with many big stars like The Who, Queen, and Madonna. He says that the problem is that there are too many small festivals and not enough well-known acts to perform at them. This makes it hard for people to attend a festival without missing out on their favorite band.

There were about 900 music festivals in the UK last year, but Goldsmith thinks that many of these will stop happening soon. He predicts that instead of big music festivals, there will be smaller events with a mix of music and other activities like poetry or magic shows.

Goldsmith also says that people's listening habits have changed. They don't want to listen to albums anymore; they prefer to focus on individual songs. This makes it harder for new rock bands to build a reputation.

At 69, Goldsmith is still working in the industry. He has teamed up with a Dutch producer to create a new theatre in London where they will stage shows that combine music and other performances.

Goldsmith also shared some stories from his past work with famous musicians like Keith Moon and John Lennon. He revealed that Elvis Presley never performed outside North America because his manager, Colonel Tom Parker, was an illegal immigrant and didn't want to risk leaving the US.

Goldsmith thinks that Queen's Freddie Mercury was one of the greatest live performers he has ever seen. However, he believes that there isn't a new band like Queen emerging in the music scene today. He says that Glastonbury festival is struggling to find new big acts and may soon reach its peak.

Two islanders found a small fibreglass boat on a remote Pacific atoll. Inside the boat was an emaciated man with long hair and a beard. He said he had been drifting for 16 months after setting out from Mexico, over 12,500km away.

The man claimed to have been adrift since September 2012, when he left Mexico for El Salvador. A companion had died at sea several months earlier. He told his rescuers that he survived by catching turtles and birds with his bare hands.

The man's condition is not good, but he is getting better. His name is José Ivan, and he spoke only Spanish. The islanders who found him took him to the main island in the atoll, where he met the mayor, Ione de Brum. Officials are awaiting more details before taking action.

José Ivan's story is unlikely, according to some experts. He had no fishing equipment on the boat, but a turtle was inside when it washed up. The boat itself looked old and worn out.

To survive at sea for so long, one needs food and water. Experts say that José Ivan would have faced major problems with exposure and dehydration. They also note that individual physiology plays a part in survival, as some people are better suited to dealing with hardship than others.

Stories of survival in the Pacific Ocean are not uncommon. In 2006, three Mexicans were found drifting near the Marshall Islands after surviving for nine months at sea on rainwater, raw fish and seabirds.

Experts have questioned José Ivan's story, saying that it is unlikely he could survive for so long without proper equipment or a clear plan. However, others note that survival stories like this are not unique, and there are many examples of people surviving against the odds in the ocean.

The European Union is introducing new rules to test car emissions in real-life situations. Up to 1 billion people will still be very poor by 2030 unless countries work to reduce inequalities. A report by the Chronic Poverty Advisory Network (CPAN) says that many people who escape poverty may fall back into it due to events like drought, illness, or conflict.

The report suggests that governments should focus on tackling chronic poverty, which affects people who have been poor for many years or their entire lives. It also recommends a "zero tripod" of objectives: tackle chronic poverty, stop impoverishment, and sustain poverty escapes.

Policymakers must aim to create a safety net through social assistance, invest in education, and implement pro-poorest economic growth policies. This will require massive global investment.

He took time to win over a rock audience but was helped by musicians like Mike Bloomfield and Eric Clapton. In the 1970s, he collaborated with Carole King and Joe Walsh on the album "Indianola Mississippi Seeds".

King became known as the "chairman of the board of blues singers" and toured internationally. He also performed at prisons and started rehabilitation programs. Despite being diagnosed with diabetes in 1990, King continued to tour but at a slower pace.

The celebrations for his 80th birthday included an award-winning album with Clapton, Knopfler, Daltrey, Estefan, and others. In 2009, he received a Grammy award for "One Kind Favor". He performed at the White House in 2012 with President Barack Obama singing "Sweet Home Chicago".

King was married twice and divorced twice. He had 11 children by different partners and passed away surrounded by his music legacy.

Kenton Cool is a famous climber who has just returned from a big achievement on Mount Everest. He climbed three of the highest peaks in the Himalayas over the course of one weekend. This is an impressive feat that few people have accomplished before.

Cool's voice is hoarse because he was climbing at high altitude, which makes it hard to talk. He and his partner reached the top of Nuptse on Saturday morning, then climbed up to Mount Everest itself in complete darkness on Sunday. On Monday, they went back down to climb Lhotse, the third peak.

Cool says that this achievement is special because there are now fixed ropes on all three mountains, which makes it easier for climbers. However, he thinks that future climbers will be able to do even more difficult climbs without using these ropes or bottled oxygen.

The article also talks about Ueli Steck, a Swiss climber who was planning an even more challenging climb before he left the mountain in April. He had been training hard and wanted to climb Everest's west ridge without any help from fixed ropes. Unfortunately, he got into trouble with some Sherpas at Camp 2 and had to leave.

The article also discusses the impact of tourism on the environment around Mount Everest. The number of tourists is increasing rapidly, which is causing problems like pollution, soil erosion, and landslides. Alton Byers, a mountain geographer, says that the combination of climate change and tourism is creating new stresses on the Sherpa homeland.

The article mentions that glaciers in the Everest region are melting quickly, which is affecting the local water supply. The town of Namche Bazaar has to lay a new pipeline to bring water for tourists, while other villages have to dig pits just outside their houses to dispose of garbage.

Byers thinks that these problems can be solved if people get serious about addressing them. He suggests that solving environmental issues like pollution and soil erosion should be prioritized over spending millions of dollars on climbing equipment or flights.

The article also talks about climate change, which is causing rapid changes in the weather patterns around Mount Everest. This is affecting tourism, as Lukla Airport is closing more often due to increased cloud cover. Byers thinks that this is a warning sign for what could happen if people don't take action to address climate change.

Byers says that Mount Everest is like a canary in a coalmine - it shows us the impact of climate change and tourism on the environment. He hopes that by studying the problems around Mount Everest, we can figure out how to solve them and make sure that this iconic mountain remains safe for future generations.

A new international survey in 33 countries shows how people misunderstand some important facts about their societies.

In Britain, people think that the richest 1% own 59% of the country's wealth. But they actually only own 23%. Americans think that 14% of their population are immigrants, but it's really only 6%. Brazilians think the average age in their country is 56, when it's actually 31.

Russians believe that 14% of their politicians are women, but it's really only 7%. In Britain, people think that many young adults live with their parents at home. But in reality, it's much lower - just 1 in 7. Indians on the internet think that most of their country has access to the internet, but it's actually less than a quarter.

So why are people so wrong about these things? Sometimes we don't understand basic math or we misinterpret questions. We might also rely too heavily on information that is easily available.

For example, many countries think that lots of people do not have a religion, when in fact most people do follow one. Our survey found that this was because people were thinking about how often they practice their faith, rather than what they said on official forms.

We also tend to take mental shortcuts and make quick guesses without checking the facts. This is why many countries overestimate the size of rural areas - we look at how much land they cover, not how many people actually live there.

In addition, our own perspectives can lead us to misunderstand how things are in other parts of our country or world. Our survey was online and might have biased towards more educated and connected people.

We also suffer from "emotional innumeracy" - we let our worries influence what we think is true. For example, many Brits overestimate the number of wealthy households and immigrants because they are worried about these issues.

However, there are some areas where people underestimate problems, like the number of overweight or obese people in their country. In Saudi Arabia, people think only 28% of their population is overweight, when it's really 71%.

Despite our misperceptions, the survey highlights interesting and important differences between countries. For instance, the top 1% own most of Russia's wealth, but very little in New Zealand. More than half of young Italians still live with their parents, while in Norway it's less than 5%. The average age in India is much younger than in Japan.

These findings show just how varied and complex our societies are - and how easy it is to get things wrong.

**Wildlife in Trouble**

Many animals are disappearing at an alarming rate. The tiger is threatened in India, orangutans are struggling in Indonesia, and pandas are endangered. But scientists now think that a bigger problem is happening closer to home - the decline of creatures like ladybugs.

Climate change, fewer animals, and more people are causing many species to become extinct. This means we might be entering a new geological age called the Anthropocene, where humans dominate ecosystems.

The World Wildlife Fund (WWF) says there's been a huge drop in wildlife numbers worldwide. Between 1970 and 2014, vertebrate numbers fell by 52%. Some species, like freshwater animals, have declined even more - by 76%.

But it's the smaller creatures that are most worrying scientists. Bees and other pollinators help us grow food, while worms clean our soil and bats control mosquito populations. Without them, we might lose a lot of crops.

Dr Nick Isaac, a scientist at the Centre for Ecology & Hydrology in Oxfordshire, says that Britain's insects and other small animals are declining quickly. He warns that this could have serious consequences for humans.

Many people rely on wild animals for food or medicine. In some parts of the world, animal food sources are a critical part of the diet, especially for the poor.

The main cause of these problems is unsustainable human consumption, which damages ecosystems and creates climate change.

WWF says there's still time to stop this decline. Its UK Chief Executive, David Nussbaum, calls it a "wake-up call" and urges everyone - politicians, businesses, and individuals - to take action to protect the natural world.

"We are a plague on earth," said Sir David Attenborough in 2013. But WWF believes we can still make a difference by protecting our planet's resources.

France's first female professional team manager has been appointed. Helena Costa is 36 years old and comes from Portugal. She graduated with a master's degree in sports science and is also a UEFA-licensed coach. Before this job, she coached several women's teams, including the Iranian women's national side.

Costa was given a two-year contract by the president of Clermont Foot 63, Claude Michy. He is known for making big headlines for his club. Some people think Costa was hired just to get attention, but others are happy about it.

Carolina Morace, an Italian who used to be the only woman coach of a men's professional team, said: "If Helena has been hired, then she must know what she's doing." Morace played for Italy 153 times and was one of the top scorers in Italy's Serie A for 12 years.

Some fans are skeptical about Costa's appointment. They think it might be just a publicity stunt or that she won't last long because she is a woman in a male-dominated sport. However, others are hopeful that she will bring new motivation to the team.

Raymond Domenech, a former manager of the French national team, said: "Women know how to play football and manage teams well. Why shouldn't they manage men's teams?" He also said he would hire a woman as his assistant if he were managing a club again.

Costa is confident that she can do her job well. She said: "Like José Mourinho, I want to win. If people compare me to him, I'm happy."

**Britain is the Loneliest Country in Europe**

According to the Office for National Statistics, Britain has more lonely people than any other country in Europe. Many British people do not have close friends or know their neighbors well. This can be a big problem because loneliness can be bad for our health.

**Loneliness Affects All Ages**

People think that only older adults are lonely, but research shows that young people are also struggling with loneliness. In fact, a survey found that 18- to 34-year-olds were more likely to feel lonely and depressed than those over 55.

**Why is Loneliness a Problem?**

Loneliness can lead to stress, depression, paranoia, anxiety, addiction, cognitive decline, and even suicide. It can also make mental health problems worse. Experts say that we need to address the underlying causes of loneliness before it's too late.

**What Can We Do About Loneliness?**

There are many things we can do to combat loneliness:

*   Use social media wisely: While social media can be a good way to connect with others, it's not a substitute for face-to-face contact.
*   Join a club or group that interests you
*   Volunteer in your community
*   Talk to someone about how you're feeling
*   Seek help from a helpline or counselor

**Help is Available**

There are many resources available to help people who are struggling with loneliness. These include:

*   Helplines like Samaritans and Get Connected
*   Online support groups and forums
*   Counselling services at work or in your community
*   Support groups for mental health issues related to loneliness

**Let's Break the Stigma Around Loneliness**

Loneliness is a common problem that affects people of all ages. By talking about it openly and seeking help when we need it, we can break the stigma around loneliness and build stronger, more supportive communities.

A team of scientists at the University of Zurich has developed a computer-assisted autopsy system called "Virtopsy". This new technique is being used in some European hospitals and could help solve crimes more easily. 

The system, which uses 3D images from MRI and CT scans, allows doctors to examine corpses without cutting them open. This can reveal injuries that were not visible during a traditional autopsy, such as internal bleeding or fractures.

Michael Thali, the director of Zurich's Institute for Forensic Medicine, believes Virtopsy could make "perfect murders" impossible. He says that with this technique, investigators can find all the evidence they need to solve a crime.

Virtopsy uses a combination of medical imaging technologies, including MRI and CT scans, to create 3D images of corpses. This allows doctors to look inside bodies without having to cut them open.

Richard Dirndorfer, one of the pioneers of DNA analysis in criminology, thinks that Virtopsy could eventually replace traditional autopsies altogether. He says this will happen gradually, just like DNA analysis replaced blood group analysis.

The new technique has already helped doctors discover haemorrhages and fractures that were not visible during conventional autopsies. It can also help forensic scientists plan their investigations more efficiently.

Virtopsy is being used in some European hospitals, including Hamburg's University Hospital. Criminologists from around the world are coming to Switzerland to learn about this new method.

The TV show CSI has already featured Virtopsy twice. In one episode, the system helped prove that a murder victim was killed by a bullet through the cheek. In another episode, Virtopsy allowed the family of a murdered man to proceed with their wish for cryogenic freezing because his body remained intact after the virtual autopsy.

Some scientists are concerned that Virtopsy could undermine traditional skills in forensic science and pathology. However, they agree that it can complement and substantiate conventional methods. 

Lars Oesterhelweg, Deputy Director of the Institute of Forensic Medicine at Charité Hospital in Berlin, says that while Virtopsy is a helpful tool, it's not yet perfect. He notes that investigators will still need to use traditional autopsy techniques for certain tasks, such as analyzing blood color or smell.

The new method can also help reopen cases where the cause of death was unclear. It allows third opinions to be gathered and investigations to be re-examined.

Relatives of the deceased often prefer Virtopsy over traditional autopsies because it's non-invasive and does not disfigure the body.

In Iceland, people are very particular about their names. The government only allows certain names on official documents like passports. If you have an unusual name from another country, the authorities might not accept it.

Tristan Cardew and his wife Kristin are having a problem with this rule. Their daughter Harriet's passport was not renewed because her name is not recognized by the Icelandic National Registry. This means Harriet couldn't travel to France on holiday until Tristan applied for an emergency UK passport from the British embassy.

In Iceland, most people have surnames that tell you who their parents are. For example, Jón Einarsson's children might be Ólafur and Sigríður. The law says that new babies' names must be submitted to the National Registry within six months of birth. If a name is not on an approved list, the parents need permission from the Icelandic Naming Committee.

This committee has strict rules about what makes a good Icelandic name. Names with letters that don't exist in the Icelandic alphabet are not allowed, and names can't conflict with the language's grammar or spelling rules. Harriet's name had this problem because of the letter "c".

Some people think Iceland's naming laws are unfair and restrictive. In 2013, a court ruled that a girl named Blær could use her given name instead of a nickname like "Girl". The former mayor of Reykjavik has also criticized the law for being silly and against creativity.

The Cardews might be able to solve their problem by giving Harriet an Icelandic middle name. However, Tristan thinks this is too late and unnecessary. He's frustrated that his family was treated unfairly because of a simple naming rule.

Google is updating maps of the Arctic region for the first time in centuries. They flew a team to Iqaluit, a town in Nunavut, Canada, to take pictures and gather information about life on the permafrost. The mission aims to help people understand what it's like to live in this remote area.

The team spent four days walking through the snow-covered terrain with a heavy backpack camera. They were helped by an Inuit expert and followed by curious locals. They took pictures of roads, homes, and shops, which will be added to Google Street View in July 2013.

Unlike other parts of the world that have been mapped using cars, the team had to hike through snowy roads and trails made of ice. They even walked on a 15km road called the Road to Nowhere, despite warnings about polar bears and wildlife.

The mayor of Iqaluit, John Graham, said the town is excited about the project. He understands why people are curious - it's a unique opportunity to explore this remote area through Google Street View.

Google faced some challenges when mapping Iqaluit, such as gathering data from satellite images and siting businesses with PO box addresses. They worked with local residents, including Inuit elders and high-school students, to correct these issues.

The project is not just about creating maps - it's also a way for the town of Iqaluit to promote itself and make planning decisions easier. The test run was successful in Cambridge Bay, another Nunavut town, last summer.

Google hopes to continue this project in other northern towns, but they are facing high costs due to shipping and airfares. They might rely on volunteers to map these areas in the future.

The leader of the project, Aaron Brindle, said he wants to see a new map of Canada's north in three to five years, with more accurate information about this remote region.

Governments in Europe are trying to find a solution to high unemployment, but some areas are still struggling. In one small town in Italy called Elmas, the mayor has an unusual idea. He wants to pay residents to leave and look for jobs elsewhere in Europe.

Valter Piscedda, the mayor of Elmas, thinks this is a good idea because many young people are leaving the town every day feeling hopeless about finding work. He believes that by paying them to go abroad and learn new skills, they will be able to get jobs and come back to Elmas with valuable experience.

The council has allocated €12,000 to pay for ten unemployed locals to take English lessons and travel to Europe to look for work. To be eligible, applicants must be between 18 and 50 years old, not be university educated, and have lived in the town for at least three years.

Some people think this idea is a good way to help those who are struggling to find work, while others think it's an admission of defeat by the government. Piscedda says he wants to give people dignity by helping them get back on their feet.

The unemployment rate in Italy is high, especially among young people under 25. In some areas, over 50% of this age group are out of work. The mayor hopes that his scheme will give those who need it the most a chance to succeed.

Some critics have said that Piscedda's plan is too expensive and that he should use the money to help people stay in Elmas instead of leaving. However, Piscedda believes that this scheme will ultimately benefit the town by bringing back experienced and skilled workers.

The unemployment rate in Sardinia, where Elmas is located, is 17.7%, making it one of the highest rates in Italy. More than half of young people are out of work, with many leaving the country to find jobs elsewhere.

Piscedda wants to give people a chance to succeed and believes that this scheme will do just that. He says he's not trying to encourage people to leave forever, but rather to help them gain valuable experience that they can use when they return.

Cities can disappear or become uninhabitable due to natural factors such as water and sand. If the planet was getting colder instead of hotter, ice would also be a threat. 

A rare "ice tsunami" in 2013 destroyed houses in Ochre Beach, Canada. However, most cities are vulnerable to rising sea levels. Venice used to flood around ten times a year, but now it floods about 100 times annually because its lowest point is only three feet above sea level.

Rising sea levels are not the only problem. In some places, the land is also sinking due to human activities like industrial exploitation. For example, Jakarta has sunk four meters in the past thirty years and is expected to continue sinking. This makes it difficult for the city's seawall to protect it from flooding.

Some cities are taking steps to address their problems, but others, such as Miami, are not admitting they have a severe environmental problem. Miami lies only ten feet above sea level and has porous limestone that absorbs rising seawater, making it difficult to drain.

In other places, rainfall is causing problems. Recently, Detroit experienced an unusually heavy amount of rain in one morning, overwhelming its outdated sewerage systems. Impoverished by the collapse of America's car industry, the city struggles to build a new system.

The Sahara Desert in Africa is expanding at a rate of 30 miles per year, threatening settlements in northern Mauritania. The desert has grown by over 260 acres around the town of Chinguetti, causing its population to decline from 20,000 people to just a few thousand.

California's Rancho Mirage may have to be abandoned due to human over-expansion and finite resources. The city uses too much water, leading to a man-made drought. A 25% cut in water consumption has been implemented, but it is unlikely to stabilize the resort.

In Japan, Hashima Island was abandoned after coal supplies were depleted. Now, sea spray is causing its concrete walls to collapse. Fire is also a growing threat to urban settlements in America and Australia due to long-term droughts making trees highly combustible.

Malé, the capital of the Maldives, has built a ten-foot sea wall at a cost of $63 million, but it may not be enough to save the city. The islands around Malé are disappearing, which could lead to Malé becoming uninhabitable. 

Some cities are fighting a losing battle against nature, and it's hard to predict natural events. However, the prospects for Malé look particularly grim due to rising sea levels and disappearing islands.

Many young adults are living with their parents because of the housing crisis. This means they can't afford to rent or buy a house on their own. A recent survey found that 20% of adults between 18 and 25 are still living at home, and many of them don't pay any rent.

The main reason for this is the high cost of renting and buying a house. Rents have never been higher, and it's hard to save enough money for a deposit on a mortgage. In fact, half of tenants can't save anything towards a deposit, and a quarter can only put aside £100 or less each month.

Some young adults are choosing to stay at home to save money, while others are being forced to do so because they can't afford to rent or buy a house. Parents who can't afford to help their children with a deposit may be willing to let them live at home for free.

A survey found that 28% of people are living at home because they're trying to save for a mortgage deposit, but 30% aren't saving any money. Some experts blame the housing crisis on older generations who have driven up house prices and rents.

Young adults like Michael Day and Jenna Gavin are struggling to afford their own homes. They're caught between paying high rents and saving for a mortgage deposit. Many of them are having to put off buying a home because they can't get a good enough deal or save enough money.

Experts say that parents may not be charging rent, but this doesn't mean they're not helping their children financially in other ways. Children who live at home may contribute by doing household chores, cooking meals, and paying for groceries.

Angus Hanton from the Intergenerational Foundation argues that older generations are to blame for the housing crisis, not young adults. He says that young people have been hit hard by falling incomes, high rents, and tight mortgage lending rules. Instead of blaming them for staying at home, we should be supporting their interests so they can afford to build their own lives.

Jenna Gavin, 29, is one example of a young adult who's struggling to save for a mortgage deposit. She wants to stay in her hometown but can't afford to rent or buy a house on her own. Her parents are happy to let her live at home and contribute in other ways.

David Bowie was a famous musician who died of cancer. Until the end, he continued to surprise people with new music and ideas. His latest album, Blackstar, came out on his 69th birthday in January 2016. It showed that he still had a gift for making exciting and challenging music.

Bowie started his music career in the 1960s as a singer-songwriter and glam-rock pioneer. He mixed different styles of music with brilliant changes of sound and image, which was rare in pop history. He was born David Robert Jones in south London and grew up to love singing and playing instruments.

When Bowie was 15, he formed his first band, the Kon-rads. Later, he changed his name to avoid confusion with another musician named Davy Jones. His first album came out in 1967, but it wasn't until 1969 that he had a big hit with the song Space Oddity.

In the 1970s, Bowie released many successful albums and singles, including The Man Who Sold the World and Hunky Dory. He became famous for his elaborate costumes and performances on stage. His album Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars was especially popular, with hits like Starman.

Bowie continued to make great music throughout his life, experimenting with different styles and genres. In 1975, he released an album called Young Americans, which included the hit single Fame. He also acted in films, such as The Man Who Fell to Earth and The Elephant Man.

In the 1980s, Bowie had a huge commercial success with the album Let's Dance and its singles Let's Dance and China Girl. He became a global rock star, touring and performing around the world. He also appeared at Live Aid in 1985 and recorded a charity single called Dancing in the Street with Mick Jagger.

Bowie married his second wife, Iman, in 1992, and they had a daughter together named Alexandria. In 2000, their son Duncan was born from Bowie's previous marriage. Bowie continued to make music until he retired for a year in 2006 due to health reasons.

In 2013, Bowie released a new album called The Next Day, which included the hit single Where Are We Now?. He received many awards and honors throughout his life, including a Grammy lifetime achievement award and induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. David Bowie is survived by his wife Iman, their daughter Alexandria, and two sons from previous marriages.

Visitors arriving at Addis Ababa airport see pictures of teff, a nutritious ancient grain. Ethiopia is one of the world's poorest countries with a difficult food situation, but it's also where teff grows.

Teff is small like poppy seeds and has lots of calcium, iron, and protein. It doesn't have gluten, making it useful for people who can't eat wheat. In Ethiopia, teff is very important and many farmers grow it. The grain is ground into flour to make injera, a flatbread that's central to Ethiopian food.

Ethiopia has been exporting teff as injera or other products, but now they want to increase production so more people can have it. A growing middle class in Ethiopia wants more teff, but this means prices are rising and many poor farmers can't afford it.

The government is trying to help by developing new teff varieties and teaching farmers better ways to grow the crop. They also want to use teff in school meals and emergency aid programs to help reduce malnutrition.

However, some people worry that increased production for export could be a problem if small farmers are not treated fairly. Right now, most of the teff grown is sold to city consumers who can afford it, leaving little for poor rural areas where teff is most valuable.

Ethiopia's government aims to double teff production by 2015 and help people in need. They want to grow more teff so that everyone, including children and adolescents, can get enough nutrients.

The Ice Bucket Challenge has raised $100 million for an American charity that helps people with motor neuron disease. The challenge also raised £4.5 million for a British charity and thousands more for charities in Hong Kong and Australia. However, not everyone is happy about this.

Some famous people are accused of showing off their bodies instead of donating money. Others think the challenge wastes water. Animal rights groups and environmentalists have criticized it too. Dan Sullivan is a 27-year-old venture capitalist who works too much and often forgets important things like dinner dates and birthdays. He has created a company called BetterBoyfriend.me that sends presents to girlfriends every month for about $70.

Sullivan's idea came from his own life. He wanted to be a better boyfriend, but he couldn't remember everything on time. So, he started a service where boyfriends can sign up to send regular gifts to their partners. The service costs around $70 per month and offers seven gift options like chocolate or manicures.

Sullivan has already made about $17,000 in revenue every month from over 350 members, mostly his friends who work at companies like Apple, Google, and Facebook. His friends signed up for the service because they wanted to be better boyfriends too.

BetterBoyfriend.me wasn't Sullivan's first idea. He also thought of a dog-sharing business where people could rent dogs out when their owners were away. However, he decided to focus on his present-giving service instead.

Another company, called InvisibleBoyfriend, offers a similar service but allows users to create a fake online partner who can text with them anytime.

Sullivan was surprised by the real relationships that have formed between his customers and the boyfriends they signed up for. Scientists in the US have created a special mirror that can help cool buildings without using air conditioning. They believe this mirror can save energy and reduce the need for power-hungry cooling systems.

Right now, 15% of the energy used by buildings in the US goes to air conditioning. But the scientists think their mirror could make some buildings so cool that they don't even need extra cooling.

The researchers tested the mirror on a roof in California. They found that while other surfaces got very hot in the sunlight, the mirror stayed around 5C cooler than the surrounding temperature.

"If you cover a big part of the roof with this mirror, it can save a lot of power," said Shanhui Fan, who led the project at Stanford University. "In some cases, you might not even need air conditioning."

The mirror is special because it reflects most sunlight and also releases heat into space through a process called infrared radiation. This means that it doesn't just reflect light, but actually cools down.

To work, the mirror needs to be attached to a surface, like a roof or a wall, so that it can cool things down by radiating heat away from them.

The scientists built the mirror using thin layers of materials, including silver and silicon dioxide. They say that the mirror could be used on buildings and shopping malls to reduce energy consumption.

In fact, one scientist said that if you use this mirror on a big surface, like a roof or a wall, it can get so cool that you might not need air conditioning at all.

The scientists are excited about their discovery because they think it could save people money on energy bills and help the environment.

A British designer, Patrick Hunt, created a cheap and safe light that uses gravity to generate power. This is similar to Trevor Baylis's wind-up radio from the 1990s. The light is powered by a dynamo attached to a 10kg bag of rocks. When the bag is dropped from a height of about 2m, it generates enough power for half an hour of light.

Hunt used crowdfunding on the US website Indiegogo to raise £400,000 in just 40 days. He was trying to get funding to start producing his invention commercially. The crowdfunding campaign allowed people to donate money and receive rewards, such as their own light.

Indiegogo is a popular platform for entrepreneurs to raise funds from the public. It has helped over 100,000 businesses and services to raise finance. Danae Ringelmann, co-founder of Indiegogo, believes that crowdfunding allows entrepreneurs to test their ideas and prove their worth to customers and fans.

Ringelmann's experience on Wall Street taught her the importance of execution and confidence when starting a business. She advises entrepreneurs to be brave and move fast, rather than being afraid of failure.

Indiegogo is growing rapidly, with about $2m raised per week for new businesses in start-up and growth stages. It has launched services in Europe and has partnerships with local card providers. Ringelmann's goal is to democratize finance and make it easier for people to access funding.

Other platforms like Kickstarter, Seedrs, and Funding Circle also offer crowdfunding options. However, Indiegogo stands out because it allows anyone to launch a campaign, regardless of how unusual the idea may be.

A British woman named Lauren Pears used Indiegogo to raise £100,000 to open a cat café in London called Lady Dinah's Cat Emporium. The site charges a 4% fee for successful campaigns and offers refunds or fees for unsuccessful ones.

JMW Turner, one of Britain's most famous painters, has won a vote to be on the new £20 note. He will be the first artist to appear on a British banknote.

The public was asked to choose a dead cultural figure who deserved this honour. Over 30,000 people suggested names, and after narrowing down the list, five artists were chosen. Turner beat these other four: Barbara Hepworth, Charlie Chaplin, Josiah Wedgwood, and William Hogarth.

Turner is famous for his dramatic paintings of the sea. He will be on a new banknote that features his 1799 self-portrait and another famous painting called The Fighting Temeraire. This ship played an important role in a big battle in 1805.

The new £20 note also has a quote from Turner: "Light is therefore colour". His signature is on the note too, taken from his will where he left many of his works to the nation.

Mark Carney, the governor of the Bank of England, said it was important to involve the public in this decision. He thinks banknotes can be a way to celebrate a country's culture and heritage.

The new £20 note will come out by 2020 and replace one that has Adam Smith on it. This is the first time the public has been able to choose who appears on a British banknote.

Police and intelligence agencies have used lie detectors, also known as polygraphs, to catch criminals and spies for almost 100 years. However, researchers in Britain and the Netherlands may soon replace them with a new method. This new method has been tested and shows a success rate of over 70%, which is much higher than the polygraph.

The polygraph measures physiological changes such as sweating and heart rate to detect lies. However, it is not very reliable and can be easily manipulated by people who are anxious or trying to deceive others. In contrast, the new method uses a full-body motion suit with 17 sensors that track movement up to 120 times per second.

The researchers' study involved 180 students and employees who were asked to either tell the truth or lie about playing a computer game or losing a wallet. The results showed that liars moved their bodies more than truthful people, allowing the researchers to correctly identify lies in 82% of cases.

One of the researchers, Professor Ross Anderson, said that the new method is promising because it can detect deception without being affected by cultural background, anxiety, or cognitive load. However, the use of all-body suits is expensive and uncomfortable, so the researchers are looking for cheaper alternatives such as motion-sensing technology from computer games.

Anderson believes that the new method could be used in police stations around the world within a decade and offers a scientifically-backed alternative to torture, which is often used to gather information but is unreliable. The research has special significance given the recent US Senate report on CIA torture.

Rebecka Singerer is an angry childminder from Gothenburg, Sweden. She got tired of being told what beer she could drink because of her sex. So, she joined a group called FemAle to make a change.

FemAle is a group of women who like drinking beer and want others to know that they can enjoy it too. They created their own beer, "We Can Do It", which is now on sale in Sweden. The beer is a pale ale with a label inspired by Rosie the Riveter, a symbol of women's power.

Elin Carlsson, 25, founded FemAle and brews cars at the Volvo factory. She says that "We Can Do It" is not just a female beer but a beer made by women for everyone to enjoy. The group wants to show that they can do things equally well as men.

FemAle has a problem: many breweries have tried to make beers for women in the past, but these were often weak and tasted differently from regular beer. FemAle's approach is different. They organize tastings where women can try new flavors and styles of beer. This way, they hope more girls will get interested in beer.

The idea for FemAle came when a group of women kept running into each other at beer festivals. One woman, Felicia Nordström, was tired of people telling her she didn't know about beer because of her sex. She teamed up with FemAle and Ocean Brewery to create "We Can Do It".

The first batch of the beer sold out quickly, and now FemAle has been approached by other breweries who want to work with them. The beer is made with three malts and two hop varieties, making it a strong but balanced brew.

"We Can Do It" uses 65 IBU (bitterness level) and has an alcohol content of 4.6%. Elin Carlsson says that women often prefer wine because they don't know what beer to order. FemAle wants to open up new worlds for them.

Some group members have changed their taste in beer over time. Singerer, 38, used to like light beers but now enjoys stout and other strong brews. The women are part of a brewing explosion in Sweden, where people are developing a passion for craft ales.

The women of FemAle say that there is no typical woman who likes beer - anyone can enjoy it. They hope that pubs will start to understand how to reach more women drinkers and that Elin has found the right way to do this.

Donald Trump is a surprising candidate for the Republican presidential nomination in the US. Despite being at the top of opinion polls, he warned that winning the election is still uncertain. 

At a rally in South Carolina with 11,000 people attending, Trump said, "Unless we win, it doesn't mean anything." He also mentioned that he wants to choose the date for the election next Tuesday.

Trump's campaign has been marked by controversy and outbursts, which some politicians might have found damaging. However, these incidents only seem to make him more popular with his supporters.

Some of the controversies include:

* Doubting the heroism of Vietnam veteran John McCain because he was captured.
* Insulting Fox News moderator Megyn Kelly for asking tough questions.
* Making negative comments about Mexican immigrants and Black Lives Matter protesters.
* Appearing to mock a New York Times journalist with a disability and falsely accusing Muslim Americans of cheering on 9/11 attackers.

Trump has refused to retract these comments, saying he is not good at apologizing. His rivals still hope that his supporters will tire of his attacks on minorities. However, one poll shows that support for Trump among Republicans has only decreased by 12 points, with him still leading the field.

Some opponents question whether Trump has any clear political ideology and if his comments are just a way to attract attention from his core constituency. Others believe that Trump's policies, such as deporting undocumented immigrants and building a border wall with Mexico, are the defining issues of the election.

One source of optimism for opponents is that polls this far away from the election day may not be accurate. Current polls show that Trump has 25-30% of the Republican vote. 

Converting Trump's passionate supporters will be hard for other candidates, as they need to tap into his support base without jeopardizing their own. Polling experts believe this is unlikely.

According to Steve Deace, a prominent Iowa conservative, Trump's antics are both good and bad. On one hand, it produces loyal followers, but on the other hand, it limits his ability to grow beyond that.

Frank Luntz, a top Republican pollster, believes Trump speaks for voters who feel like they have a mouthpiece and want to be heard. They agree with him because he says what they think, even if it's outrageous.

The Star Wars franchise has been around for over 38 years, taking audiences to a galaxy far away with its iconic characters and stories. Even in 2015, when a new film was about to be released, fans were still very excited. Paul Dergarabedian, a media analyst, said that it's hard to imagine another movie franchise that can evoke such passion and enthusiasm.

In 2012, Disney bought the rights to Star Wars from its creator, George Lucas, for $4 billion. This deal included plans for new movies and spin-offs. One of these spin-offs is about Han Solo, a character played by Harrison Ford in the first three films. The movie is scheduled to be released in May 2018.

In December 2015, a new Star Wars film called "The Force Awakens" will be released, directed by JJ Abrams. It will be followed by another film in 2017 and a spin-off called Rogue One in 2016. Rogue One will tell the story of a rebel mission to steal the plans for the Death Star.

Rumors that Rogue One might feature Darth Vader again have made fans very excited. This suggests that people still love the original series and are eager to see more. Lucasfilm-Disney is using this success to create a bigger universe around Star Wars, similar to what Marvel Studios has done with its successful films.

To build excitement for new movies, Disney has made all six existing Star Wars films available on streaming services. This has helped keep fans engaged and interested in the franchise.

The level of enthusiasm for Star Wars has been high for over two decades. Fans have created a wide range of content, including novels, comic books, video games, and merchandise. Event-cinema companies like Secret Cinema in the UK have even used live performances to bring people together to watch Star Wars movies.

Michael Rosser, a news editor for Screen International, thinks that this "shared universe" of nostalgia is what keeps Star Wars so popular. He believes that new films will reconnect with the original series and be successful because they go back to Han Solo and Luke Skywalker's storylines.

Despite not being well-received by critics, the prequels (three films made between 1999 and 2005) still made a lot of money at the box office. This shows how powerful the Star Wars brand is. Rosser also thinks that movie studios are trying to ensure the quality of new movies and bring people back to cinemas.

Dergarabedian predicts that "The Force Awakens" will have a record-breaking opening in December 2015 and make over $1 billion worldwide. He believes that Star Wars is the ultimate movie brand, and its popularity won't fade soon.

In 2010, the old city in Srinagar was a difficult place for police to visit because separatists were fighting for an independent Kashmir. Many people were killed or injured during these fights. However, today tourists can walk freely in the same streets, eating food and taking pictures.

Srinagar is now a popular tourist destination with many visitors from around the world. In 2002, only 27,000 tourists visited the area, but in 2012, almost one million people came to visit. Omar Abdullah, the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, wants more British tourists to come to the area.

However, the UK's Foreign Office still advises against visiting Srinagar because it is considered a high-risk area. This makes it difficult for people from the UK to get travel insurance if they do decide to visit. Omar Abdullah believes that this advice is unfair and that many other countries are safer than Jammu and Kashmir but are not given the same warning.

Abdullah says that tourists can be safe in the state as long as they take normal precautions, such as avoiding areas near the border with Pakistan. Many local people agree with him and welcome tourism as a way to boost the economy. However, some visitors may worry about the ethics of having fun in an area where many people are suffering from anxiety and mental health problems.

To improve tourism, Abdullah wants to invest in better infrastructure, roads, and electricity. He also wants to attract more big-spending tourists by offering them more things to do in the evenings. Some local Islamic groups have advised foreign tourists to dress modestly when visiting Srinagar, but Abdullah believes this is not a problem.

Jammu and Kashmir's finances are in a difficult state after many years of conflict. The state receives very little money from taxes, but pays out a lot on salaries for public employees. Omar Abdullah hopes that tourism will help to improve the economy and attract more visitors to the area.

James Hamblin, an editor from The Atlantic magazine, tried something unusual to understand how often we should shower. He didn't take a shower for some time and stopped using shampoo and soap when he did. This experiment helped him learn that washing our bodies too much can actually make us feel dirtier in the long run.

When we shower, we wash away the natural oil and good bacteria on our skin. This makes our skin work harder to restore its balance, which can lead to more oil being produced and an unpleasant smell. On the other hand, not showering as often allows our skin to recover and produce healthy oils and bacteria again.

Hamblin found out that giving up soap and showers for a while has several benefits. Our skin becomes healthier, and we might even see improvements in conditions like acne and eczema. This approach can also help the environment by reducing water waste. In fact, an average shower uses 65 litres of clean water every seven minutes.

Clean water is becoming harder to find, especially in places like California that are experiencing droughts. Using fewer soap products and showers is a simple way to make a positive impact on our planet.

If you're worried about body odour when giving up regular showers, don't be. Many people still use deodorant or wash their hands with soap regularly to stay clean and healthy. Hamblin's experiment shows that finding a balance between cleanliness and letting our skin breathe is possible. So, try reducing the number of your daily showers and see how it makes you feel!

Moses King, a 48-year-old man living in Liberia, has been struggling to take care of his family since he was diagnosed with HIV. He had access to antiretroviral medication but couldn't afford the right food to eat. As a subsistence farmer, he grew vegetables and bought rice, but meat and fish were expensive and hard to get.

Pate K Chon, a counselor who works with people living with HIV in Liberia, came up with an idea to start a fish farm after watching a documentary about a similar project in Thailand. She wanted to provide work and access to protein for people living with HIV.

Chon started building a pool for the fish farm with the help of John Sheehy, a philanthropist who raised money for the project. The fish farm, now called Grow2Feed Liberia Fish Farm, has 12 tanks that can hold up to 200,000 fish per year. The community will benefit from the fish and also use waste from the tanks to irrigate crops.

The project is special because it's a co-operative, meaning the people living with HIV in the community are part of it. They work on the farm or tend to the crops and get fish in return, which they can eat or sell in the market. This gives them a way to earn money and feed their families.

Good nutrition is very important for people living with HIV. Research shows that they need more protein to stay healthy. However, food is expensive in Liberia, and many people struggle to afford it.

Grow2Feed Liberia Fish Farm is the first co-operative fish farm in Liberia to operate for the benefit of an HIV-positive community. The project has attracted attention from the Liberian government and the UN Food and Agriculture Organization.

Fish farming experts say that this practice has huge potential in Africa, where many people rely on imported frozen fish that is not good quality. Good practices can mitigate problems like inbred fish and toxins.

Sheehy hopes to replicate the model throughout Liberia and other countries in West Africa. He believes that his project can help improve nutrition and food security for people living with HIV and others who struggle to afford healthy food.

For 85 years, Pluto was shown as a grey blob on maps of the solar system. On July 15th, NASA's New Horizons spacecraft sent back high-resolution images of Pluto and its large moon Charon. These images showed dramatic mountain ranges made from solid water ice, similar to those found in the Alps or Rockies.

The team behind the mission was thrilled with the results. Alan Stern, the principal investigator, said the data were "amazing" and that Pluto and Charon were "mind-blowing". One of the biggest surprises was discovering mountains in the Kuiper belt, a mysterious region where Pluto resides among 100,000 smaller icy objects.

The images showed that the surface of Pluto has been recently smoothed over by geological activity. This could be due to geysers or cryo-volcanoes that erupt ice into the atmosphere. Scientists were also surprised to find that the mountains on Pluto are made from water ice with a thin layer of methane and nitrogen ices.

The close-up region covers only about 1% of Pluto's surface, but it suggests that the planet is still geologically active. The images show that Pluto's surface is smooth, which could be due to internal heat or snowfalls covering the surface.

New Horizons flew by Pluto at a distance of 5 billion kilometers, taking hours to send back a single picture. It will take 16 months to send all the data it has collected during the fly-by. The team also announced that they would name the heart-shaped feature on Pluto after Clyde Tombaugh, who discovered the dwarf planet in 1930.

The new view of Charon reveals a varied and complex terrain, with cliffs, troughs, and a deep canyon estimated to be 7-9 kilometers deep. Scientists are excited about the possibility of studying these objects further, which could help explain the formation of the Earth and other planets.

New Horizons will continue its journey into the Kuiper belt, potentially opening up new windows on the ancient solar system. The mission is expected to run until the mid-2030s, when it will shut down due to a depleted plutonium power source.

A former president of the Royal Institute of Navigation, Roger McKinlay, thinks we rely too much on GPS technology. He believes that if we don't use our natural navigation skills, they will disappear.

McKinlay says we need to invest more money in developing better navigation systems before technologies like self-driving cars can become a reality. In the meantime, he wants schools to teach children how to navigate using maps and other traditional methods.

According to a study from 2009, people who used to be taxi drivers but are no longer working behind the wheel perform worse on navigation tests than those who still drive taxis. This suggests that our navigation skills can decline if we don't use them regularly.

Neuroscientist Dr Hugo Spiers agrees with McKinlay that relying too much on GPS technology is a problem. He says there's a risk of getting into dangerous situations because of satnav errors, like the case of a driver who drove into a reservoir in Spain in 2010.

Spiers also thinks that how we use navigational technology can affect its impact on our brains. For example, using smartphone apps as digital maps requires us to think more about where we're going and interact with the device. This is different from following audio instructions, which removes the need for thinking.

McKinlay believes that navigation technologies still have a long way to go before they can be used in critical applications like flying planes or navigating aircraft. He's also skeptical about the development of artificial intelligence-based navigational aids, saying it will take more than just making machines smarter.

Ultimately, McKinlay thinks humans need to remain able to navigate on their own, without relying too much on technology. "Technology isn't magic," he says. "It's just a tool."

**Feeling Glum About Work? Think Again!**

Are you feeling unhappy about your job in January? You're not alone. But before you start looking for a new one, let's put things into perspective.

We spoke to five people who do unusual jobs and asked them about their salaries, the worst parts of their jobs, and what they like about their work.

**1. Dog-Food Taster**

* Job: Taste dog food to make sure it meets quality standards
* Salary: £20,000 (entry-level), up to £50,000 for experienced technical directors
* Worst part: Tight deadlines and sometimes smelly job sites
* Satisfaction: No two days are the same, and he likes helping pets become happier and healthier

**2. Hygiene Technician**

* Job: Disinfect areas that have been exposed to bio-hazardous situations (e.g., crime scenes, hoarders' houses)
* Salary: £14,500 (entry-level), up to £22,000
* Worst part: Cleaning up after suicides and dealing with disgusting sites
* Satisfaction: Variety of tasks, pride in transforming hazardous sites into safe environments

**3. Biogas Engineer**

* Job: Setting up biogas plants in developing countries
* Salary: £10,000 (entry-level), up to £30,000 for chief technical officers
* Worst part: Seeing people struggle with poverty and dealing with smelly anaerobic digestion processes
* Satisfaction: Helping communities increase incomes, improve health and hygiene

**4. Eel Ecologist**

* Job: Conserving the critically endangered European eel
* Salary: Not specified
* Worst part: Working with tricky eels, learning about environmental damage caused by humans
* Satisfaction: Working outdoors, seeing British wildlife up close, and helping river systems and coastal habitats

**5. Shopping Channel Presenter**

* Job: Selling products on live TV
* Salary: £30,000 (trainee), over £55,000 for experienced presenters
* Worst part: Unsociable hours, including weekends and late evenings
* Satisfaction: Live presenting, thinking on feet, and knowing viewers are ordering products

These jobs might not be for everyone, but they're definitely interesting! Who knows? You might just find a new passion or career path.

Google Unveils Driverless Car

Google is testing a new driverless car that can take people where they want to go without anyone driving it. The car has no pedals or steering wheel, but instead uses a smartphone app to navigate and stop. It's like catching a chairlift by yourself - you just sit back and relax.

The company is building 100 of these cars to test them over the next two years. They're electric and have special foam at the front to protect people in case of an accident. Google says they want to make roads safer, especially for people who can't drive themselves.

However, some people are worried that driverless cars will replace human drivers and cause unemployment. In London alone, there are 22,000 licensed black cabs and about 100,000 taxi drivers.

Other car makers like Volvo, Ford, and Mercedes are also working on similar technology, but it's not as advanced as Google's version. The director of Google's self-driving car project says they're still learning and adapting their cars to make them safer and more reliable.

So far, the Google driverless cars have covered 700,000 miles without any accidents caused by the computer. But they still have a long way to go before they become widely available.

Valdevaqueros beach in southern Spain is a peaceful place where surfers fly over the waves on kites. The beach has been untouched for many years, but it's now facing a big change. The local council wants to build a huge tourist complex with 1,400 hotel rooms and 350 flats right next to the beach.

Many people are against this plan because they think it will harm the environment and the animals that live there. Environmental groups say that the project will damage the habitats of protected species, such as birds and bats. They also worry about the impact on the famous Levant wind, which attracts surfers from all over the world.

The council says that the project is necessary because many people in Tarifa are out of work due to Spain's economic crisis. The town has 18,000 inhabitants, but 2,600 are unemployed. A councillor named Sebastián Galindo said that tourism is the only way for the town to survive, as long as it's done sustainably.

However, opponents of the project say that it will bring more problems than benefits. They point out that Spain already has a million empty homes and that building new housing will make things worse. They also worry about the noise, pollution, and destruction of the beach and its surroundings.

The campaign to save Valdevaqueros beach was launched immediately after the council voted for the project. The campaign is supported by groups such as Greenpeace and Birdlife. They say that the resort would be like putting a shopping centre in the middle of the Alhambra, a famous historical site in Spain.

Some people also think that the complex should be built elsewhere, such as on wasteland near the town's old centre, rather than next to the beach. The Andalusian College of Geographers says that the proposed site overlaps with protected areas and wildlife conservation zones.

Raúl Romeva, a member of the European Parliament, said that the project is at fault because it doesn't take into account environmental directives and urban laws. He also pointed out that Tarifa already suffers from water shortages in the summer.

Many locals agree that the complex should be built to create jobs, but they want it to benefit everyone in the town, not just a few people. They think that building on wasteland near the old centre would be a better option.

A biologist named Aitor Galán said that Valdevaqueros is an important place for wildlife and that building there would destroy its unique features. He compared the project to turning Benidorm into a resort, but with worse consequences.

Scientists have created a special map of the brain called an "atlas" that shows how words and their meanings are arranged in different parts of the brain. This atlas is like a colorful picture book that helps us understand how our brains work when we think about language.

The scientists wanted to create a giant map that would show how one important part of language, called semantics (the meaning of words), is represented in the brain. They used special imaging techniques to record brain activity while people listened to stories on a radio show. The researchers then matched the transcripts of the stories with the brain activity data.

The atlas shows that no single spot in the brain represents just one word or concept. Instead, each word activates many different spots in the brain, which work together to represent its meaning. For example, the words "life", "love", and "death" all light up different networks of brain cells.

This research could have a big impact on medicine and other fields. It could also help people who are unable to speak due to certain diseases, such as motor neurone disease or locked-in syndrome. The scientists hope that their work will lead to the development of a language decoder that can allow these people to communicate through a computer.

The atlas is based on data from seven people who listened to 25,000 words while in a scanner. The researchers found that the brain maps were similar for all participants, but it's likely that people from different backgrounds and cultures will have different semantic brain atlases.

The scientists are now working on new atlases that show how the brain represents other aspects of language, such as numbers, syntax (the rules of grammar), and narrative structure. They hope to create a more comprehensive and precise semantic brain atlas in the future.

Experts praise the research for shedding light on how the brain works in real-world scenarios. However, there are still many things to learn about how semantics is represented in the brain.

Key points:
